characters.name: Patrick Star
characters.description: Adimwittedpink starfish who isSpongeBob'sbest friend for life. He isnormally unemployed, but has held a variety of day jobs throughout the course of the series. Despite hisgoofy behavior,he can occasionallyshow hints of brilliance. Clickhereif you want to see him describe himself. Abandoned Catchphrase: In the first three seasons, he would exclaim "Good morning, Krusty Krew!" upon entering the Krusty Krab, though this hasn't been said by him since "Mid-Life Crustacean" (though wasborrowedbySpongeBobin "Bummer Vacation" and by Mr. Krabs in "Bottle Burglars"). Abusive Parents: Patrick mentions in the episode "Home Sweet Pineapple" that he was permanently kicked out of his parents' house at a young age. However, he reunites with his real parents at the end of "I'm with Stupid", implying that he has no hard feelings towards them despite what they did. Accidental Truth: In the episode "Patrick-Man!", he starts attacking patrons at the Krusty Krab, believing that one of them is a supervillain in disguise. When Mr. Krabs is about to throw him out, it turns out that the Dirty Bubble was in fact there in disguise.

characters.name: Plankton
characters.description: A tiny planktonic copepod with a Napoleon complex. With the help of his computer wife Karen, he runs the failing Chum Bucket restaurant across the street from the Krusty Krab. He is always after the secret Krabby Patty formula and dreams of running the Krusty Krab out of business. If you’d like to hear Plankton describe these tropes himself,click here. Abandoned Catchphrase: In "Plankton!" and "Culture Shock", whenever his plans failed, he'd reply with, "Well, this stinks." However, starting with "F.U.N.", Plankton gave up on this phrase, though he's started using it again in some newer episodes. Abusive Dad: Towards his and Karen's son Chip in"Karen's Baby". As Plankton never wanted a baby, he spends most of the episode going out of his way to avoid showing any affection towards Chip, including showing up his baby form's attempts to walk, refusing to help him stop crying and eventually outright telling his teenage form to run away. It takes Karen threatening to throw Plankton out if he can't find his son and said son's first word being "father" before Plankton finally accepts him as his son. Affably Evil: He's shown to be quite polite at a few points in the series, which is a sharp contrast toMr. Krabs. This is best exemplified in the end of"Wishing You Well": Plankton, having been granted his wish to be taller, now towers over everybody and could smash the Krusty Krab if he felt like it. Instead, he jovially greetsSpongeBoband Mr. Krabs before rampaging through the city, leaving them and the Krusty Krab completely unscathed.

characters.name: Karen
characters.description: A waterproof supercomputer who runs the Chum Bucket alongside her husband Plankton. She is always giving him new evil plans to steal the Krabby Patty formula, but their efforts never succeed. Karen is Plankton's own invention, and her software is built into many of his machines. Actually Pretty Funny: Sometimes laughs with the good guys against Plankton. Affably Evil: Even more so than her husband. She is married to an unabashed villain and occasionally aids him in stealing the Krabby Patty formula, but is otherwise on decent terms with most of the cast. All There in the Script: Her name wasn't mentioned at all in the "Plankton!" episode, but it was listed in the credits. Armless Biped: In the movie and most episodes from season 5-9, her mobile form does not have arms. From season 10 onwards, however, her mobile form always has them.

characters.name: Sandy Cheeks
characters.description: An athletic, thrill-seeking squirrel from Texas who loves her home state. She works as a scientist and lives in an underwater dome full of air. She usually wears a bubble-helmet diving suit when she is outside of her home. Academic Athlete: She qualifies even if the show is not set in a school. She's probably the most academically inclined character with a vast knowledge of science, and also aPassionate Sports Girlwho excels at karate. Action Girl: Much more so in earlier episodes, though it still shows through every now and then. It's often shown that she's very strong, occasionally so much that she easily defeatsSpongeBob, as tough as he is to damage, in Kung-Fu battles. Americans Are Cowboys: The only character explicitly stated to come from the United States, and she's a Texas cowpoke through and through. Animals Not to Scale: She's rather small for a squirrel. InSponge Out of Water, she's smaller than a human's foot.

characters.name: Mrs. Puff
characters.description: SpongeBob's patient but paranoid teacher at boating school. She would like nothing more than to passSpongeBobsince he is an obsessively good student, but he routinely freaks out and crashes whenever he has to get inside a boat. She is a pufferfish who blows up into a ball whenever she is scared or stressed out. Alliterative Name:PenelopePuff. Apathetic Teacher: Zigzagged,Depending on the Writer. Though it's mostly her attitude towardsSpongeBobsince no matter what she does, she can't seem to get him to pass the driving portion of her test and out of her hair for good. His over-eagerness certainly doesn't help, neither does continually landing her in jail either. Ax-Crazy: In "Demolition Doofus" when she becomes obsessed with attempting to getSpongeBobkilled in a demolition match, and tries to kill him herself when that fails. Big Beautiful Woman: Her size comes with a noted appetite for pasta and cake, but she handily attracts Mr. Krabs, andSpongeBob'smotherhas to talk loudly to pull her husband's attention off of her.

characters.name: Pearl Krabs
characters.description: Mr. Krabs' beloved teenage daughter, who is a huge sperm whale. Her brain is the largest in Bikini Bottom and she is gifted in math, but she is still young and immature. Her father hopes to pass his restaurant on to her when she grows up. Acrofatic: Justified. She's a whale, so of course she'd be agile for her size. All Girls Like Ponies: In "Whale of a Birthday", Pearl spots a mini seahorse at the mall and expresses herAnd Call Him "George"attitude towards it by sitting on it tightly, much to the seahorse's discomfort. All of the Other Reindeer:Depending on the Writer, she tends to have a reputation among her peers as the social outcast. Ambiguously Related: Her biological relationship to Mr. Krabs isn't mentioned. It's unknown if she'sadoptedor whether she takes after herMissing Mom.

characters.name: Gary the Snail
characters.description: SpongeBob's pet snail, who meows like a cat. Advertised Extra: Despite his prominence in advertising, most of his appearances boil down to minor gags with actual Gary-centric episodes beingvery rare. Affectionate Nickname: He callsSpongeBob"PapaBob" in "Chatterbox Gary" when he gets a translator for his meows.SpongeBobalso calls him "Gare Bear" quite often. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: Is a turquoise snail with a bright pink shell. Animal Jingoism: In "Pets or Pests", he develops a mutual hatred for a wormSpongeBobtakes in, since worms in this show are the undersea equivalent of dogs.

It has been used somewhat more frequently since then. Also, inone episode, he even has an entire award closet that floods out ahugepile of awards when opened by Patrick. The one task he'sbadat is driving, as Mrs. Puff can attest, and even then it’s hinted that he’s only bad at it because he feels pressured by Mrs. Puff. Achievements in Ignorance: In "House Sittin' for Sandy", he spends quite a while in Sandy's treedome without a helmet and manages not to dry up until Patrick visits andreminds him that the treedome is filled with air. Accidental Truth: In "Funny Pants", after getting annoyed bySpongeBob's non-stop laughing

characters.name: Mr. Krabs
characters.description: Abandoned Catchphrase: He liked to say "You're fired!" in the early episodes, but this was dropped after Season 1. Abusive Parents:Zigzagged.He often neglects Pearl in post-movie episodes, and his miserly ways cause her no small level of grief, thoughPearl does have her moments where she gets the last laugh(often in the form of using the cheap crustacean'sMoney Fetishagainst him by blackmailing him with money). This contrasts sharply with his original portrayal; in very early episodes like "Culture Shock", he is shown to care for Pearl more than his money. That said, more recent post-movie episodes have found a balance between the two: Krabs is still a total miser, but he does love Pearl more and can even become overprotective in order to ensure she’s happy and safe. Accidental Pervert:In "New Digs", Mr. Krabs thought it wasSpongeBobbehind the shower curtain, but it was actuallySpongeBob'smom. characters.name: Harold and MargaretSquarePants
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Originally only appearing every now and then when the plot called for it, they started appearing a lot more in Season 13 onwards with an increasing number of plots involving them. The reason for this is presumably Nickelodeon trying to market towards their younger Gen Alpha viewers, who are children who live with their parents.noteOriginally,SpongeBobwas supposed to be a child in boating school, with his parents and teacher being recurring characters, as most Nickelodeon shows at the time focused on schoolchildren. Stephen Hillenburg pushed so hard to make him an adult with a job, so a compromise was made in that he attends boating school instead while still being a working adult. Crazy Jealous Guy: In "New Digs", Mr. Krabs pulls down a shower curtain that Margaret is behind, thinking that it wasSpongeBob, she shrieks and he apologizes repeatedly and backs off, but Harold doesn't take this well. Given Name Reveal: "Whelk Attack" reveals that Margaret's maiden name is "BubbleBottom". Good Parents: They really adore their son, even allowing him to stay at their place after he loses his home, and buying him a boatmobile after he gets his driver's license. Happily Married: They are always seen together and seem really happy with each other.

characters.name: GrandmaSquarePants
characters.description: SpongeBob's paternal grandmother. The Bus Came Back: After 12 years of absence, she finally returns in Season 14’s “Don’t Make Me Laugh” with Marion Ross reprising her role. Cool Old Lady: In the comic "Great Grandma", she's not only aSupreme Chef, but she's a modern dance aficionado, she collects rare clarinet records, and she's a talented painter who is also skilled at making homemade paint. Covered in Kisses:SpongeBobgets covered with kissing marks by her on an implied regular basis. Granny Classic: At least in her first appearance, where she dotes onSpongeBobby feeding him milk and cookies, knitting him a sweater with love in every stitch, and reading him stories.

characters.name: GrandpaSquarePants
characters.description: SpongeBob'sgrandfather, who is only mentioned bySpongeBobbut never physically appears outside of a thought bubble. Brick Joke:SpongeBobhad anImagine Spotrecalling what GrandpaSquarePantssaid about flying before deciding to build a flying machine. A few minutes later, after seeingSpongeBob's plan, Patrick mentions whathisgrandpa used to say... with hisImagine Spotbeing GrandpaSquarePantsas well!GrandpaSquarePants:If we were meant to fly... Hey!(pokes Patrick with his cane)I'm notyourgrandfather! Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Well, he never appeared on-screen in present-day, but he hasn't even been mentioned since Season 3. Comically Missing the Point: WhenSpongeBobfirst wishes he could fly, he recalls how his grandpa said if they were meant to fly, they'd have propellers on their heads or jet engines on their backs. Rather than see this as his grandfather deterring a pursuit of the impossible,SpongeBobtakes it as advice to build a flying machine. Driving Up a Wall: According to his grandson:SpongeBob:I guess GrandpaSquarePantswas right. Don't run for a bus.(imitating GrandpaSquarePants)"Especially one that's going up at a 90° angle!"

characters.name: Shelley
characters.description: SpongeBob'spet scallop, who lives in a cage in his bedroom. All There in the Manual: Her name and gender are only revealed in the "Bikini Bottom's Up Tour", a special feature on Disc 3 of The Complete 1st Season DVD. When the viewer selects her cage, Patchy talks about her and says that her name is Shelley while also confirming she's a female. Ambiguous Robots: Paul Tibbitt said on Twitter that he sees Shelley as an automaton like a singing bird box, but in the "Bikini Bottom's Up Tour", Patchy talks about her like she’s a living pet. Birdcaged: Shelley lives her entire life in her cage and has only been proven by absence to escape twice. In "TheSpongeBobMovie: Sponge Out of Water", Shelley's cage was empty and there was a big hole in it and "SpongeBob'sPlace", her cage was full of money and she was not present. Forgettable Character: Episodes such as "A Pal for Gary" and "Rock-A-Bye Bivalve" seem to completely deny the existence of Shelley, even though she is physically seen in background shots of those very episodes.

characters.name: Stanley SquarePants
characters.description: SpongeBob's clumsy cousin who destroys everything he touches. Ambiguous Family Ties: We don't know exactlyhowSpongeBoband Stanley related — it's unclear if Stanley is Uncle Sherm's son or his nephew. He calls him "Uncle Sherm" instead of "dad", but he could simply be saying that forSpongeBob's (orthe audience's) benefit. Biting-the-Hand Humor:Stanley:Wow! A TV! Uncle Sherm never let me watch TV back at home.SpongeBob:Why not?(the TV explodes)Stanley:That's why.(runs off)What's that?SpongeBob:Oh, it's okay. There's nothing good on television anyway.(turns to camera and frowns)Nothing. Bridal Carry: A picture depicts Stanley (in a groom's tuxedo) doing this to a customer (in a bridal dress). Dragged into Drag: Stanley takes a mock wedding photo with a male customer as the bride, much to the latter's annoyance.

characters.name: BlackJack SquarePants
characters.description: SpongeBob's badass, sociopathic cousin who would very often challenge him to fights before being arrested. Ambiguous Family Ties:BlackJackandSpongeBobare paternal first cousins, butBlackJack's father isn't directly stated. He's implied to be Blue's son, given that they live right next door to each other (and if they were, it would be a case ofLike Father, Unlike Son, given that Blue is a retired police captain andBlackJackis an ex-convict), but they could just be uncle-and-nephew. The other possibility is that his father is an unnamed and unseen brother of Harold and Blue. Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking: As much as he tormentedSpongeBobin their youth and is an all-around thug, he ultimately served ten years in jail after littering. Big Brother Bully: Or rather "Big Cousin Bully". He very often psychologically and physically tormentedSpongeBobin his childhood years by exploiting his cowardliness. Disproportionate Retribution: He was sentenced to ten years in prison for...littering.

characters.name: Captain Blue SquarePants
characters.description: SpongeBob's paternal uncle, who is a retired police captain. All for Nothing:SpongeBobgetting forced to work menial chores by Uncle Captain Bluefor hours until dusk. Also doubles as torture. It finally stops whenSpongeBobpulls the plugon Blue's record player and finally makes him listen. Armor-Piercing Question: AskedSpongeBobthis question...Uncle Captain Blue:Do you have any idea what people like that do to people like you? Da Chief: Well, a retired one, anyways. Dirty Coward: AbandonsSpongeBobto confrontBlackJackon his own, anddrives off.

characters.name: Sherm SquarePants
characters.description: Consolation World Record: His biggest claim to fame is being able to fit an entire watermelon up his nose, at least according toSpongeBob. The Ghost: Never appears directly on-screen save for a few photograph cameos. Nose Shove: Has a watermelon in his nose. Resentful Guardian: Justified. Sherm is fed up with his son Stanley's inability to hold down a job and the fact that he is irresponsible and ruins everything he touches, so he sends him to his nephewSpongeBob's house in an attempt to straighten him out. Notably, on the letter he sends toSpongeBob, aFreeze-Frame Bonusshows him having written "I'm free, FREE!", indicating Stanley was driving him crazy. Strong Family Resemblance: Is yellow and square like his nephewSpongeBob, and even has buckteeth (albeit many more thanSpongeBobhas) and a similar outfit (albeit with a bowtie instead of a necktie). This is particularly notable as his brothers and mother are more round and brownish-colored like real sea sponges.

characters.name: Patrick’s parents (pre-Patrick Star Show)
characters.description: Patrick's parents, as portrayed beforeThe Patrick Star Showoverhauled their characters. The Cameo: They reappear in "Rule of Dumb" on Patrick and Gary's family tree as well as "Patrick's Tantrum". Cruel to Be Kind: In "Home Sweet Pineapple", Patrick mentions that they got tired of him and kicked him out of the house so he could learn to live by himself. The Ditz: Not to the extent of Patrick, but they're pretty clueless, since they apparently spent the majority of their debut asking Squidward where their son was, without thinking to just go next door likely even after Squidward told them. Like Parent, Like Child: "I'm With Stupid" happens not only because Patrick thought two strangers were his parents, but because Herb and Margie got lost on their way to Patrick's house and kept bothering his neighbor Squidward about where their son is. On the other hand, they're amazed that Patrick recognizes them at the end and that he remembered to get dressed.

characters.name: Cecil and Bunny Star
characters.description: Patrick's parents, as portrayed from the premiere ofThe Patrick Star Showonwards. Adaptation Dye-Job: The original version of Patrick's parents were both pink like him, but Cecil and Bunny are teal and lavender respectively. Adaptation Name Change: They were originally known as Herb and Margie in the main show, but in Patrick's spinoff, they are renamed Cecil and Bunny. Amazing Technicolor Population: Cecil is blue-green while Bunny is purple. Animal Facial Hair: Despite both of them being starfish, Cecil has a prominent mustache, and as shown in "Dad's Stache Stash", Bunny has a very slight one.

characters.name: Squidina Star
characters.description: A member of the Science Scout troop who goes with Sandy to the moon. She is shown to have a bit of a rivalry with Pearl, as the two tease each other over their choice in social cliques. Doubles as a both a science-loving nerd and a comic book-lovinggeekwho loves playing with action figures too much. She's a main character in the spin-offThe Patrick Star Show, as Patrick's younger sister and the executive producer of his show. Alliterative Name:SquidinaStar. Animal Jingoism: She's a squid who has a small rivalry with Pearl, a sperm whale.They eventually become friends. Animals Not to Scale: She's implied to be aGiant Squidbased on her head shape andrelationship with Pearl, yet stands shorter than a squirrel (at least at eye level). To make things more confusing, her head fins also technically make her taller than Squidward,a fully-grown cephalopod, despite being a kid. Ascended Extra: Squidina had only made two appearances inSpongeBob SquarePants(one supporting, one minor) prior toThe Patrick Star Show, which made her the deuteragonist. Even those appearances could be considered a case of this, as Squidina is a redesign ofIncidental 11, a background character notable only for aNon-Standard Character Design(given she was a squid and most other incidentals are fish).

characters.name: GrandPatStar
characters.description: Bearded Baby: If "The Lil' Patscals" is any indication, he had a beard even as a boy. Butt-Monkey: He has it better than the other Stars, but he sometimes has his fair share of misfortunes. Childhood Friends: "The Lil' Patscals" establishes that he, Granny Tentacles, and Old Man Walker were close friends as children. Cruella to Animals: In "10 & 1 Toilets,"GrandPattries to disassemble Tinkle's toilet puppies and use their parts to relive his glory days as a toilet-themed fashion designer. Dad the Veteran: He’s a former member of the Marines.

characters.name: Agnes Steelhead
characters.description: Evil Matriarch: Agnes not only burns down Granny Tentacles' house because she thinks it's "ugly", but convinces Squidina thatshewas the one who did it. She alsomakes Bunny's house dirty right after she cleans it, can barely remember Cecil's or Patrick's names, and sends the latter aVoodoo Dollof him with nails impaled in it. Flying Broomstick: Being a witch, she flies around on one. Foil: ToGrandPatStar. Both of them are Patrick and Squidina's grandparents, but whileGrandPatis a wrinkly, flabby old man who deeply cares for his family beneath his grouchy attitude, Agnes is a fairly shapely, attractive older lady who doesn't get along with her family at all to the point of being abusive to them. Four-Legged Insect: Like the other squids in the franchise, she only has six tentacles. Gruesome Grandparent: She's not very nice to her grandson Patrick (or her son-in-law Cecil and his fatherGrandPat, for that matter), which turns Squidina against her in her debut episode.

characters.name: Sam Star
characters.description: Alliterative Name:SamStar. Baritone of Strength: A freakishly strong girl with a rough, deep, masculine voice. Big Sister Instinct: She's violently protective of Patrick. The Ditz: She's even more stupid than her brother, and that's saying something. Dumb Muscle: She's far dumber and far stronger than Patrick.

characters.name: Rocky
characters.description: Companion Cube: He's a pet rock and therefore an inanimate object that Patrick treats as if it were alive and sentient. Dark Horse Victory: With Gary out of the race and Snellie forfeiting to be by his side, the real winner of the race is... Rocky, which somehow got to the finish line. Morality Pet: Patrick is shown to genuinely care for and love Rocky, despite the fact that he can be a jerk at times (even by Season 3 standards). Slow and Steady Wins the Race: WhileSpongeBoband Squidward bring normal snail pets, Patrick brings Rocky. It predictably doesn't move while the other snails race forward, but Gary (SpongeBob's snail) went berserk and runs out of the race line and injures himself in the end, while Squidward's snail (who's close to winning) runs to Gary instead to help him. While everyone (including the spectators) is distracted with the 2 snails, it then cuts to Rocky somehow crossing the finish line.

characters.name: Ouchie
characters.description: Patrick's pet sea urchin inThe Patrick Star Show. All Animals Are Dogs: He barks like a dog to communicate, despite worms already being the dog stand-in. Eyeless Face: He's depicted with no visible eyes. Meaningful Name: His name alludes to his painful spikes. Sea Hurtchin: He’s regularly the cause of injuries for his owner and others.

characters.name: Tinkle
characters.description: A sentient toilet with teeth whom the Star family treat as a pet. All Animals Are Dogs: And some sentient objects are too, apparently. Tinkle’s voice and behavior are largely doglike. Animate Inanimate Object: A living toilet who serves as a pet for the Star family. Butt Biter: Temporarily picks up this habit in “The Drooling Fool”. Depending on the Artist: Tinkle's teeth change depending on the episode. In some, like "Gas Station Vacation" and "Uncredible Journey", he only has teeth when biting or growling. In episodes like "Family Plotz", he always has a visible row of teeth even when his mouth is closed. In "10 & 1 Toilets", he is always drawn with small fangs even when his mouth is closed, but the full row of teeth when his mouth is open.

characters.name: Mrs. Tentacles
characters.description: Abusive Parents: To a degree, she is verbally abusive to her son. In "Fools in April", she screamed at her own son "YOU STINK!". She also famously insulted him in "Sportz?", by giving him somewhat of an invertedyour mominsult. In "Scavenger Pants", she joked that she only had one child because "One of him [Squidward] was enough." One issue ofSpongeBob Comicsreveals that the weakness of Squidward’s superhero persona is his mother calling him a disappointment. Ambiguous Situation: Whether she and Squidward's dad are still married or divorced is unclear. Her mailbox has "Mrs. Tentacles" written in it rather than "Mr. and Mrs. Tentacles", indicating she lives alone, which combined with the fact that Squidward's parents never appear at the same time further implies that they separated, but "Jeffy T's Prankwell Emporium" portrays Squidward's dad Jeffy as a travelling salesman, making it possible that he just travels all the time and that's why he doesn't live at home much. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Her appearance in her debut episode, "Fools in April",depicted her with white puffy hair, lipstick, and eyelashes without any visible wrinkles◊, whereas her later design makes her look visibly older while giving her lavender hair, glasses, and gold earrings. She would be redesigned yet again in "Momageddon", having darker hair and a slightly younger appearance (likely because she looked too similar to Granny Tentacles). The Faceless: The flashback to Squidward's infancy in theKamp Koralepisode "Kamp Kow" only shows her and Squidward's dad from the waist down. Non-Mammalian Hair: She has hair despite being an octopus.

characters.name: Granny Tentacles
characters.description: Squidward's grandmother, who lives in a teapot house and is capable of making chum edible by making fricassee from it. Several years before Squidward attempted to sell her recipe at the Chum Bucket, Granny Tentacles lived across the street from the Stars. She would regularly butt heads with Patrick and his family sinceThe Patrick Showwould often interrupt her sleep. Granny Tentacles was also in a relationship withGrandPatStar, Patrick's grandfather, having known him since childhood when she was a member ofGrandPat'sgang, the Kelp Bed Kids. Ascended Extra: BeforeThe Patrick Star Showcame along, Granny Tentacles only made one physical appearance inSpongeBob SquarePants.The Patrick Star Show, on the other hand, promotes her to a supporting character. Bait-and-Switch Comment: She makes these sorts of comments on the regular, saying something sweet and innocent before completing the sentence with something mean-spirited. Butt-Monkey: Just like her grandson, she is constantly picked on by the world around her, and the Stars won't give her a break. Whether or not it's karmic depends on the writer, though.

characters.name: Jeff Tentacles
characters.description: Ambiguous Situation: Whether he's still married to Mrs. Tentacles or divorced is unclear. Squidward's mother lives in a very feminine-decorated with "Mrs. Tentacles" written in the mailbox rather than "Mr. and Mrs. Tentacles", indicating Jeff no longer lives there. But given his characterization as a travelling prank item salesman in "Jeffy T's Prankwell Emporium", it's possible that he just travels a lot and so is rarely at home. Depending on the Artist: Each of his appearances gives him a completely different style. Depending on the Writer: His early appearances implied that he was very similar to his son in personality, quiet and stuffy. In a later appearance, he's reimagined as a jovial prankster who sells pranking items. Early-Bird Cameo: Like Sandy and Plankton's fathers, he appeared in the bookHooray for Dads!long before actually debuting on the show. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: His first appearance in "Momageddon" depicted him with a dull greenish color and gloomy expression similar to his son, in addition to a brown mustache, only two strands of hair on his head and his only clothing being a pinkish shirt and a magenta sweater vest. Just one season later in "Jeffy T's Prankwell Emporium", he's a brownish yellow color and established with a more humorous personality, plus his mustache is now gray, he has eyebrows as well as hair at his temples, and his clothing is changed to a full brown suit with shoes and a green bowtie with purple polka dots. In theHooray for Dads!picture book that predated his first physical appearance in the show, he was nearly identical to his son aside from having slightly more greenish skin, a darker brown shirt and wearing glasses as well as a necktie.

characters.name: Snellie the Snail
characters.description: Absent Animal Companion: Never appears after "The Great Snail Race" (although an identical snail belonging to Mrs. Puff appears a few episodes later in "The Sponge Who Could Fly"). Fun with Homophones: When Squidward boasts that Snellie is a purebred, Patrick thinks he said the snail is made of bread. Ship Tease: With Gary. Speedy Snail: A very fast racing snail, though she forfeits the race to be by Gary's side.

characters.name: Cheeks Family
characters.description: Badass Family: They make their debut by fighting off a gang of rattlesnakes in order to save Sandy andSpongeBob. Early-Bird Cameo: Pa appeared in the bookHooray for Dads!long before his television debut. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Pa Cheeks' depiction in theHooray for Dads!storybook essentially resembled his daughter with gray eyebrows and a mustache as well as a cowboy hat, with a photo depicted in "Surf N' Turf" depicting him as scrawnier and clad in overalls and a bandana beforeSaving Bikini Bottom: The Sandy Cheeks Movieredesigned him to be overweight with a brown mustache and clad in a red one-piece swimsuit with a yellow star on the chest. The Engineer: Randy demonstrates his share of technological know-how and tries to showSpongeBobthe ropes when they repair the family's vehicle. Even the Guys Want Him: Randy is so attractive and charismatic that his wink has won him multiple contests and he even makesSquidwardfaint at the end of the film.

characters.name: Sandy's nieces
characters.description: Bratty Half-Pint: Very small, and very annoying and entitled. Chaste Toons: Are Sandy's nieces who need to be babysat by her andSpongeBobin their debut episode. The Dividual: They all have the same voice, personality, character design, and finish each others sentences. Expy: Three identical mischievous siblings who finish each others' sentences and are only distinguishable by the color of their clothing? Sounds likeHuey, Dewey and Louie. Hated by All: Due to the chaos they cause, the are disliked bySpongeBob, Patrick and Sandy. Even their own mother was unhappy to see them.Sandy:I tried to tell ya the first rule of babysitting my nieces.SpongeBob:What's that?Sandy:Don't babysit my nieces!

characters.name: Wormy
characters.description: Sandy's pet caterpillar, who turned into a butterfly. Artifact Name: Despite being a caterpillar, he's still called "Wormy". After he metamorphosed into a butterfly, that only made him less like a worm than before. A Dog Named "Dog": A caterpillar (often colloquially referred to as a worm) named Wormy. The Dreaded: Inadvertently becomes this toSpongeBob, Patrick and the rest of Bikini Bottom when he transforms into a butterfly overnight, causing mass hysteria even though he's harmless. Jump Scare: Whenever someone stares at Wormy, it's usually accompanied by a sudden closeup of a buzzing horsefly following by anyone who saw Wormy screaming and running away.

characters.name: Krabs family
characters.description: Mr. Krabs' extended family, including his grandmother, Great-Aunt Sally, unnamed sister, triplet nephews, and his ancestors. Chaste Toons: Mr. Krabs' unnamed nephews are this for a one-off gag. Though oddly enough, Mr. Krabs himselfdoeshave a daughter (though this could've been done because his daughter is a whale). Estranged Soap Family: None of Mr. Krabs' extended family shows up for Pearl's birthday parties or even Mr. Krab's wedding with Cashina.Grandpa Redbeard doesn't even know who Pearl is and thought she was a "hideous sea monster." Expy: Mr. Krabs' nephews are one ofHuey, Duey, and Louie, beingidentical tripletswho solve mysteries. Generation Xerox: All of Mr. Krabs' ancestors had rivalries with Plankton's ancestors. King Krabs even has a whale daughter

characters.name: Betsy Krabs
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: She wasfuriouswhen she thought Plankton was just using her to get the Krabby Patty secret recipe. Brave Scot: She speaks with a slight Scottish accent in later appearances, and has enoughBeware the Nice Onesmoments to make one wary of her. Good Parents: She seems to be a loving, fair, but firm mother to Mr. Krabs and also is willing to disciplineSpongeBoband Patrick on occasion. Larynx Dissonance: In her first two appearances, she sounds like a man due to being voiced by Paul Tibbit. Nightmare Fetishist: Much to Mr. Krabs' embarrassment, Betsy was really looking forward to watching Patrick get mauled by a lionfish.

characters.name: Victor Krabs
characters.description: Early-Bird Cameo: His picture appears in "Gullible Pants" well before he makes his first physical appearance in the series. Lazy Bum: At the end of "Momageddon", he lazes around withSpongeBoband Squidward's dads Harold and Jeff, demanding that his son get him some krabby patties. Non-Mammalian Hair: He's a crab with a mustache.

characters.name: Captain Redbeard
characters.description: Mr. Krabs' paternal grandfather, who works as a pirate. Arc Words: Captain Redbeard lives by the pirate's code of honor: "Never tell a lie." Captain Colorbeard: His name is a typical pirate captain's name, but a rathermisleadingone, since while he himself is red, his beard is gray (though it may have been red when he was younger). Disappointed in You: Captain Redbeard was disappointed to hear that Mr. Krabs wasn't actually a real pirate. Not because he went against thefamily businessbut because he lied. Dressed to Plunder: Captain Redbeard is always in his pirate uniform.

characters.name: Great Grandpop Krabs
characters.description: Mr. Krabs' great-grandfather. Grandparental Age Dissonance: As Mr. Krabs himself is implied to be middle aged (if not a senior citizen), it's a wonder that even hisgreat-grandfather is still alive. Long-Lived: Still alive, albeit just barely, despite the fact his great-grandson is an old man. Scatterbrained Senior: His mind evidently isn't all there, as when Mr. Krabs summons him to fight against Old Man Jenkins and his family, all he says is "Ooh, respect someone". Senior Citizen's Even Older Parent: Exaggerated. His son, grandson, and even great-grandson are old men.

characters.name: Mr. Doodles
characters.description: The pet worm of Mr. Krabs, who has made three small, blink-and-you'll-miss-him appearances. All Animals Are Dogs: Like all worms in theSpongeBobuniverse, Mr. Doodles is the undersea equivalent of a dog. Mr. Doodles barks, pants, sniffs things, and likes going for walks. Animal Jingoism: Averted. In "Gary & Spot", Mr. Doodles was shown partying with Gary. Cat/Dog Dichotomy: Or in this case, Snail/Worm Dichotomy, and it's averted. Mr. Doodles is actually good friends with Gary and they never argue or fuss because of their species. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Mr. Doodles quietly stopped appearing in the show after the Season 3 episode, "As Seen on TV". Even episodes that took place mainly in Mr. Krab's home didn't show even a trace of his existence. However,he finally returned to the seriesin the Season 12 episode, "Gary & Spot".

characters.name: Ma and Pa Plankton
characters.description: Chubby Mama, Skinny Papa: Pa Plankton is thin while Ma Plankton is obese. Early Installment Character-Design Difference:Ma Plankton in her debut in "Something Narwhal This Way Comes" resembles a cyclopic version of the one-shot character Ma Angler from "Trenchbillies". For later appearances, she looks more like an overweight version of her son with dark blue hair, a purple dress and orange-framed glasses.Pa Plankton's first depiction in the picture bookHooray for Dads!has him resemble his son with a brown mustache and eyebrow as well as wearing a Hawaiian shirt, in addition to having a blue pupil and olive skin. For the actual show, he's redesigned to resemble his son with a gray beard, a red cap, a white shirt and tattered overalls. In addition, "A Plankton Family Tree" (aSpongeBob Comicsstory that came afterHooray for Dads!was published while predating his first physical appearance in the show) depicted him as looking like a rounder version of his son with two eyes, a nose, tentacles and gray temple hair and a mustache. Ma Plankton in her debut in "Something Narwhal This Way Comes" resembles a cyclopic version of the one-shot character Ma Angler from "Trenchbillies". For later appearances, she looks more like an overweight version of her son with dark blue hair, a purple dress and orange-framed glasses. Pa Plankton's first depiction in the picture bookHooray for Dads!has him resemble his son with a brown mustache and eyebrow as well as wearing a Hawaiian shirt, in addition to having a blue pupil and olive skin. For the actual show, he's redesigned to resemble his son with a gray beard, a red cap, a white shirt and tattered overalls. In addition, "A Plankton Family Tree" (aSpongeBob Comicsstory that came afterHooray for Dads!was published while predating his first physical appearance in the show) depicted him as looking like a rounder version of his son with two eyes, a nose, tentacles and gray temple hair and a mustache. Non-Mammalian Hair: They have hair and a be

characters.name: Lily Plankton
characters.description: Plankton's grandmother. Dirty Old Woman: In "Grandmum's the Word," Lily falls in love with Squidward, a man who is much younger than her, and at one point imagines having him as a slave. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Lily seemingly had two eyes (as evidenced by her glasses having two lenses) instead of one like the rest of her family in her debut appearance, but subsequent appearances depict her with one eye instead. Given Name Reveal: Lily's first name wasn't revealed until "Grandmum's the Word." Grandparental Age Dissonance: Barely turned 90 in "Grandmum's the Word", despite Plankton being the exact same age as Mr. Krabs, which ispresumablymiddle-aged or old.

characters.name: Granddad Plankton
characters.description: Plankton's grandfather. The Bus Came Back: Returns 14 years later in Season 14, albeit only making a minor cameo appearance. Eaten Alive: Was apparently eaten by a whale at some point in his life. Nightmare Sequence: Appears in Plankton's nightmare along with other relatives at thebottom of a whale's stomach. Non-Mammalian Hair: A copepod with a beard.

characters.name: Plankton's cousins
characters.description: Plankton's hillbilly cousins. He contacts them in an attempt to raise an army so he can get the secret formula to the Krabby Patty. Ambiguously Evil: Plankton'sEvil Geniusrelatives show up alongside his hillbilly relatives in later episodes, but they don't actually try to do anything villainous. Comically Missing the Point: Despite the rest of the family panicking about Mr. Krabs' cookbook claiming Krabby Patties contain plankton as an ingredient, Clem doesn't react because he can't read the cookbook. Mr. Krabs tells him to buzz off and he does. Country Cousin: Most of Plankton's (known) cousins are hillbillies, in sharp contrast to theevil geniusinventor that Plankton is.Plankton:I've been away from home longer than I thought... Early Installment Character-Design Difference: If you take the mascots ofUnited Plankton Picturesas early versions of them, they are very different. Several of the original versions had two eyes, horns and no legs.

characters.name: E.M.I.L.P.
characters.description: Karen's mother and Plankton's mother-in-law. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Has not appeared since her debut. Fun with Acronyms: E.M.I.L.P.,EmergencyMother-In-LawProgram. Mama Bear: Is very protective towards her daughter Karen, and angry at Plankton when he made her cry. Obnoxious In-Laws: She complains about Plankton and wishes that Karen could have married an ATM, who is someone with money.

characters.name: Spot
characters.description: An amoeba who Plankton adopts from the animal shelter. He becomes a sidekick to Plankton and Karen, as well as the third resident of the Chum Bucket. All Animals Are Dogs: Spot barks, goes for walks, and is capable of protecting his owner from danger, just like a dog. The Bus Came Back: Spot returns in the aptly named Season 11 episode "Spot Returns" and has made sporadic appearances since. Collection Sidequest: He's a collectible bonus character in every level ofThe Cosmic Shake. Morality Pet: To Plankton. Caring for the amoeba really brings out Plankton's nicer side.

characters.name: Chip
characters.description: Karen and Plankton's computer son. Ancestral Name: Karen chose to name him Chip after her grandfather. Baby's First Words: He's mentally a teenager when he says his first cuss word, but still recently made when he says his first word, "father". Calculator Spelling: He starts off as a calculator as a baby. When Chip starts crying, she quiets him by typing "4445"; then turns it upside down, which says "Shhh". Delivery Stork: A robot stork delivers Chip as a baby.

characters.name: Mr. Puff
characters.description: Answer Cut: Mr. Krabs asks, "What happened toMr.Puff?" Cut to live-action footage of a pufferfish used as a lampshade.SpongeBob:She doesn't like to talk about it. The Bus Came Back: After being gone forover two decades, he finally returns in Season 14's "Hysterical History" in a flashback story told bySpongeBob. Expy: In "Hysterical History", he resembles Henry Ford and his Model C Boat is a parody of the Ford Model T. Noodle Incident: His fate. All we know is that he's a lamp now and Mrs. Puff "doesn't like to talk about it". Posthumous Character: Was killed and turned into a lamp sometime before the series started.

characters.name: Anette
characters.description: All There in the Manual: Her name was confirmedin a 2019 Instagram postfrom Nickelodeon Latin America. The Bus Came Back: Well, kind of. She makes a cameo appearance as a photo on Mrs. Puff's wall in "Spot Returns" and "My Two Krabses." Cat Up a Tree: Gets stuck up a tree, only for the branch she's on to break. Fortunately,SpongeBobcatches her just in time. Reused Character Design: Has an identical design to Squidward's snail Snellie from a couple episodes prior.

characters.name: Mrs. Puff's peanut worms
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Food: Mr. Krabsmistakes them for actual peanutsand attempts to kidnap themwhen searching for food to steal from his friends' houses. Informed Species: Obviously, they look nothing likeReal Lifepeanut worms, orsipuncula. Pun-Based Creature: Are worms who look like peanuts. Toilet Humour: One of them squirts water at Mr. Krabs when he attempts to steal it, which is supposed to be a family-friendly innuendo for squirting pee.

characters.name: Patchy the Pirate
characters.description: The host of the series' special episodes. He is a live-action pirate portrayed by Tom Kenny, the voice ofSpongeBob. He is the president of the fictionalSpongeBobfan club. Alliterative Name:Patchy thePirate. Breakout Character: Following his debut in the Christmas show, Patchy became the host of severalSpongeBobspecials and marathons following his debut, as well as appearing on some Nickelodeon commercial segments. He even makes a guest appearance inBig Time Rush! The Bus Came Back: He returns in "Feral Friends" after years of only appearing in commercials and in stop-motion form ("It's aSpongeBobChristmas!"). Butt-Monkey: The guy's a loser, according to the Narrator. His role in the specials is nothing but slapstick and being constantly thrown under the bus. He is also subjected to many cartoonish injuries in the segments featuring him, such as being exploded in "Party Pooper Pants" or attacked by aT. Rexin "Ugh".

characters.name: Potty the Parrot
characters.description: Patchy's obnoxious, wisecracking pet parrot who is depicted as a crudely-made marionette puppet with very obvious strings and googly eyes. Alliterative Name:Potty theParrot. Ambiguous Gender: Potty lays an egg in two episodes, is directly referred to asherandshein the tie-in chapter books, and has a name that parodiesPolly(a female name). However, Patchy sayshiswhen referring to Potty's voice in "Friend or Foe," and gender pronouns are never used for the character elsewhere. In 2017, showrunner Vincent Waller confirmed inin a tweetthat "it is only a puppet, with no tell tale signs of gender". Bratty Half-Pint: Rare adult version of this trope (in this sense of being developed enough to lay eggs). An obnoxious parrot that messes with Patchy's show. Characterization Marches On: In their first appearance, Potty behaved more like a real parrot such as repeating minimal phrases and single words. In all later appearances, Potty becomes more responsive and talks human-like. Potty's first appearance shows the parrot as either being less intelligent orObfuscating Stupidity. Potty makes its annoyance at Patchy and higher intelligence obvious in later episodes.

characters.name: French Narrator / "Frenchy"
characters.description: A scuba diver with a camera who narrates episodes off-screen as if they were nature documentaries about the ocean. He is aShout-OuttoJacques Cousteau, the famous oceanographer and filmmaker whose work was an influence on series creatorStephen Hillenburg. The episodeFeral Friendsmarks the first time the French Narrator makes a major appearance. A Day in the Limelight: He plays a major role inFeral Friendswhere he was called by Sandy to explain the weird phenomenon that has turned her friends into actual marine lifeforms. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": He doesn't have a real name, and is solely known as the French Narrator. Horror Host:The Tidal Zone, an event occurring between the mainSpongeBobshow and its two spinoffsKamp KoralandThe Patrick Star Show, was presented by him in a style similar to howRod SerlinghostedThe Twilight Zone (1959). Mock Cousteau: The French Narrator is intended as an homage toJacques Cousteau, narrating the antics of the title character and those around him as if they were part of a marine biology documentary and with a marked French accent.

characters.name: Flying Dutchman
characters.description: An old pirate who died a long time ago, but instead of being buried, he was used as a window display. As a result, he never found peace and continues to haunt the seas as a ghost, often aboard his ghostly ship. Ambidextrous Sprite: There's a ragged hole in the brim of his hat that tends to favor the side facing the viewer, and will often switch places throughout the episode. Bad Is Good and Good Is Bad: He shows shades of this in "The Legend of Boo-kini Bottom", as he describes Halloween as theworstholiday after describing the things he likes about it and assuresSpongeBobthat he is inbadhands. And then there's howSpongeBobdefeats him by letting him inside his mind and frightening him with theSugar Bowlwithin. Big Bad: He is the main villain in the video gameRevenge of the Flying Dutchman, attempting to makeSpongeBoband his friends his crew afterSpongeBobunwittingly set him free of his bottle prison. He's also the main villain ofThe SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants. Big Bad Ensemble: OfTitans of the Tide, alongside King Neptune.

characters.name: King Neptune
characters.description: The ruler of the sea, whose crown is his prize possession and holds his symbol of authority over all his undersea kingdom. While he has a completely different design and voice from the series,Word of Godhas said that they consider him interchangeable with the main series Neptune. Adaptational Jerkass: The series' Neptune, while still aJerkassand indifferent to mortals, ispretty affableand a far more understanding monarch, isn't as possessive towards his belongings, and treats his subjects far more pleasantly. This Neptune, by contrast, is a tyrannical, punishment-obsessed, and ill-tempered king (compared to his more compassionate daughter, Mindy). He tends to freak out and overreact over the slightest wrongdoings and considers himselfJudge, Jury, and Executioner; he refuses to believe Mr. Krabs when he maintains his innocence and is eager to fry him on the spot. Despite his iron-fisted rule over the sea, horrible temper, and obsession of harsh punishments by executing people or sentencing them to the dungeon, he manages to learn his lesson at the end, finally listening to Mindy and accepting her advice at being a more compassionate ruler. Adaptational Wimp: It's complicated. Sure, the movie Neptune is very much a threat, but compared to his canon counterpart in the TV show—who has literal god powers (asTitans of the Tideshows) and truly lives up to his Roman God of the Sea title by having his own domain to live in—the movie version is much more of a king whose location can be easily found by anyone. Along with that, he doesn't have any powers beyond his trident, even despite towering over most of the movie's cast. And even then, his trident is more mechanical than magic. Always a Bigger Fish: It’s the sole reason he’s afraid of Shell City and the Cyclops who guards it. He towers over Mindy and the other sea creatures, but is only about knee high to a human. Baldness Angst: He's so concerned with covering his baldness that he doesn't notice Plankton taking over Bikin

characters.name: Larry the Lobster
characters.description: A handsome, muscular lobster that gets all the girls. Almost always seen at Goo Lagoon or in crowd shots. Alliterative Name:Larry theLobster. Ambiguously Related: A line of dialogue in "SpongeGuardon Duty" implies he was raised by a (now elderly) fish couple, though it is never elaborated on in any other episode.noteMade even more confusing in "Patrick-Man!", which reveals that the lady fish is apparently the Dirty Bubble in disguise. Beware the Nice Ones: A pretty friendly guy, but not someone you'd want to angerconsidering his size, which Squidward learns in "Squid Plus One". The Big Guy: He's a lifeguard with a muscular physique.

characters.name: Realistic Fish Head
characters.description: As the name suggests, a realistic tuna who works as an anchorman and announcer. His partner, Perch, acts as a field reporter. He is featured in the opening sequence, and he narrates the in-universeMermaid Man and Barnacle Boyshow. Demoted to Extra: His appearances after season 4 dwindled, averaging roughly one appearance per season (in seasons 6, 7, 8, and 9) in favor of anchor Perch Perkins, who also serves the reporter role. In fact, most of his appearances past this point even have him pass duties onto Perch Perkins midway through reporting. Non-Standard Character Design: He's represented as a photograph of an actual fish in a traditionally animated cartoon.And he mentions he's aware of itin "The Fry Cook Games". Only Known by Their Nickname: He only introduces himself as "Realistic Fish Head." He has had a plethora of given names in throwaway lines and tie-in media: Elaine, Mr. Fish, Johnny, and evenT. McTroutof Trout TV News.

characters.name: Perch Perkins
characters.description: An on-the-scene news reporter in Bikini Bottom. He is the co-worker of the Realistic Fish Head. He was created for the first movie and eventually made his way into the main series. Alliterative Name:PerchPerkins. Canon Immigrant: He was originally created for the first movie, but later became a recurring character in the series proper (albeit with a different color scheme due to a firewall between Paramount and Nickelodeon, which was eventually lifted). Casual Danger Dialogue: Perch Perkins usually seems to be completely unfazed by the terrible things going on in the world, as he does a news report on them and just continues to sport that newsworthy smile as he happily tells his viewers what horrifying disaster is befalling the city.Perch:Mr. Plankton, we've received a word that you're plotting to infiltrate the Krusty Krab and steal the Krabby Patty secret formula. [shoves Plankton a microphone to speak into] Is that true? Coincidental Broadcast: Perch Perkins does news reports on topics that just so happen to conveniently move the plot of the episode along.

characters.name: Jellyfish
characters.description: The show's analogy of bees, jellyfishes inhabit Jellyfish Fields, although they occasionally wander to other places. Jellyfishing, the activity of capturing jellyfishes using nets, isSpongeBoband Patrick's favorite hobby. Their progenitor is the King Jellyfish, a huge jellyfish wearing a crown and cape. Bee Afraid: They are a bee equivalent, after all. Expect someone to get zapped by their sting whenever they appear. Beware the Cute Ones: Jellyfish may be cute but they sting like the dickens and many of them have been proven to be violently dangerous, putting characters like Squidward in traction ("Jellyfishing") and giving Dr. Manowar a gigantic permanent blemish that hurts when it's touched ("I'm Your Biggest Fanatic"). Big Bad: Queen Jellyfish in "Jellyfishing". Bullying a Dragon:SpongeBob, Patrick, and other "jellyfishers" do this as an everyday hobby, walking straight up to deadly, weaponized animals and catching them in nets.

characters.name: Bubble Bass
characters.description: An obese, picky fish, and the main antagonist of Season 1 episode "Pickles", who was built up as a recurring nemesis toSpongeBobin the first season. After a long absence, he returned as a common patron of the Krusty Krab and regular character starting in season nine. Acrofatic: Avertedhard. Bubble Bass is shown to haveStout Strength, but his weight frequently causes him problems and if he has to move fast, he often ends up completely exhausted from the stress. In "Pickles" he's shown pathetically wheezing for dear life as he manages a weak jog to run away from the Krusty Krab; and his running in "Bubble Bass Reviews" shows him desperately winded. Aesop Amnesia: Bubble Bass is so immature and selfish that even though he regularly faces consequences for his actions, he refuses to learn from them. In "Bubble Bass's Tab" he smugly starts a new tab at the Krusty Krab after the customers chipped in to bail him out of his current one just to get him out of the restaurant. No matter how many times it's spelled out to him that everybody in Bikini Bottom hates him for his unpleasantness, he still is so egotistical thathe acts like he's superior to everyone and that the whole town loves and respects him. Alliterative Name:BubbleBass. Animal Motifs: In newer seasons there is frequently a piglike squeal when he reacts to something, fitting his nature as a corpulent, greedy, gluttonous and filthy asshole. Ironically, in "The Big Bad Bubble Bass" he plays a parody of the Big Bad Wolf in his quest to steal a toy of a pig-themed superhero.

characters.name: Kevin C. Cucumber
characters.description: An obnoxious sea cucumber, whoSpongeBoband Patrick formerly admire and idolize. Alliterative Name:Kevin C.Cucumber. Asshole Victim: He constantly gets injured when he tries to getSpongeBobhurt.And he gets the fronds on his head torn off at the end of his episode. It should beBody Horror, but he deserved it for the massive jerk he was being. Bad People Abuse Animals: He smacks the first jellyfish that flies intoSpongeBob's net and kicks 20 others that do the same.These result in him getting stung. The King Jellyfish's reaction to seeing him implies he's done worse. Beard of Sorrow: In "Mooned" he is seen with a long unkept beard after being thrown out of the Jellyspotters and living in a trash can for who knows how long.

characters.name: Fred
characters.description: An accident-prone fish seen in various episodes to say hisfamous catchphraseaftersomething bad happens to him. This character model's name has varied; in most appearances from seasons 1 to 10, he was nameless, with the exception of "Patty Hype" in which he is called Fred in a 2-second throwaway line. His name was given as Clint in "Big Sister Sam" from season 7. In season 10, the new showrunners re-adopted the name Fred after seeing it on fan-made wikis, mistaking it for a fan-created name. Ascended Extra: Originally just a background character, Fred rose to prominence in "My Leg!", which wasall about him. Since then, Fred has not been forgotten as he's made plenty of supporting roles in future episodes, not as a background character, but as just another member of the recurring cast. He'd still be referred to by name, he'd have meaningful interactions and relationships with the other characters, and he was just one of the guys. Borrowed Catchphrase: Before Fred officially became the designated "My Leg" guy in Season 11, earlier episodes would feature other background characters getting hurt and saying "MY LEG!". Breakout Character: Easily one of the most popular minor characters of the series thanks to his hilariousButt-Monkeystatus and tons of his dialogue becoming memes such as "Rev Up Those Fryers", "DEUAAAAAUGH", and of course, "MY LEG!". Butt-Monkey: With as much misfortune he suffers from episode to episode, there's a reason he says "My leg!" so much.

characters.name: Mama Bass
characters.description: Bubble Bass's mother who is weary of her son's immaturity. Abusive Parents: Downplayed; while most of her appearances show her nagging at and berating her son, and even attacking him on a few occasions, most of the time, it's only when he is being an ass and is doing something that warrants discipline. How she is with him is largelyDepending on the Writer. Acrofatic: Like her son, she's obese, but unlike her son she has a lot more physical stamina and can pull off some impressive feats for her weight. It's eventually shown she and her son are talented tango dancers. Characterization Marches On: As time has gone on, Mama Bass's relationship with her son has seen some changes from episode to episode.Her earlier appearances in "Moving Bubble Bass", "Swamp Mates", and "The Big Bad Bubble Bass" established her as someone sick of her son's sponging off of her and being a lazy bum in her basement, fully acknowledging what a nightmare he is and having little patience for his antics.Later appearances like "Momageddon", "Tango Tangle", and "Bubble Bass Reviews", however, have her still being happy to spoil her son and treat him like a baby, which is something he greatly enjoys since it means she does everything for him. Examples include making snacks for him on a whim, making him drink from a baby bottle, keeping him on an almost literal leash if he wanders away from her, and even being in a mother-son tango team with him. That said, even "Bubble Bass Reviews" mostly consists of her trash-talking him for being such a pathetic shut-in despite her being established as making him snacks and coddling him as a "special boy". Her earlier appearances in "Moving Bubble Bass", "Swamp Mates", and "The Big Bad Bubble Bass" established her as someone sick of her son's sponging off of her and being a lazy bum in her basement, fully acknowledging what a nightmare he is and having little patience for his antics.

characters.name: Slappy
characters.description: A very creepy and eccentric fish. Ascended Extra: He started out as an occasionally recurring character in the main series, butThe Patrick Star Showgave him a more significant and frequent role as aLoony Fanof Patrick's show. Big Eater: His debut episode has him swallow an entire cake whole. Cloudcuckoolander: He demonstrates some very weird behavior, especially inThe Patrick Star Show. One example is in "Terror at 20,000 Leagues", where he responds to his Halloween costume being insulted by offering broccoli to the child who did so and wishing them a healthy Halloween. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: For his debut in "SpongeBob's Big Birthday Blowout", he had yellow skin, orange lips and wore a black suit. For later appearances in both the main series andThe Patrick Star Show, he is now colored green with pink lips and his suit is brown.

characters.name: Old Man Jenkins
characters.description: A ridiculously old man, who owns a farm. Ascended Extra: Although he was initially just a character who would make recurring gag appearances, he's overtime become somewhat of a breakout character, who's now being given notable roles in multiple episodes. Barefoot Loon: Old Man Jenkins doesn't wear shoes, even when he goes to restaurants. Beware the Silly Ones: Old Man Jenkins may seem like a harmless old goat, but he can drive other people crazy with his annoying old man powers and being a senior, he's pretty much societally immune to any adult younger than him disrespecting him back because you know, "Respect Your Elders". Breakout Character: Originally, the name "Old Man Jenkins" was just a name given to every single senior citizen around Bikini Bottom, which would be used whenever a gag involving an old man came into play. However, these old men all became really popular with fans to the point, where they wanted to see at least one of the Old Man Jenkinses to become a character. The writers recognized this and thus began the birth of the recurring old farmer guy, we now know as the official "Old Man Jenkins".

characters.name: Old Man Walker
characters.description: A confused and discombobulated old man, whose naivety gets him kicked around by the world. Ascended Extra: Originally appearing as just a background character, Old Man Walker has now started having more supporting roles in certain episodes. Blind Without 'Em: Actually, he's still pretty blind with 'em too. As seen in "As Seen on TV", Old Man Walker seesSpongeBoband tells him "I saw you on TV last night.", only for a flashback to reveal that Old Man Walker was actually just watching a commercial with a yellow cereal box. Butt-Monkey: Old Man Walker is occasionally the victim of physical violence and slapstick gags. Cloudcuckoolander: Old Man Walker seems to be suffering from dementia, causing him to act rather buffoonish and make variousnon-sequiturcomments, whenever he's on screen.

characters.name: Squilliam Fancyson
characters.description: Squidward's rival from high school. Squilliam is essentially everything Squidward dreamed of being. Whereas Squidward is a middle-class jackass stuck in a dead end job and considered a joke by everyone exceptSpongeBoband Patrick, Squilliam is a successful, filthy stinking rich jackass beloved by all. Also, unlike Squidward, who has had a fewPet the Dogmoments over the years, he appears to have no redeeming qualities whatsoever. He loves rubbing his success in Squidward's face. The Ace: Is way more successful compared to Squidward. Alliterative Name: Applies to his German dub name, Siegbert Schnösel. Alpha Bastard: Squilliam tends to use the fact that he is rich to look down on others, especially Squidward. He loves to taunt Squidward as well. Always Someone Better: He'sfarmore successful than Squidward ever was or will ever hope to be.

characters.name: Marina
characters.description: Pearl's friend, who works at the mall restaurant, Hot Dog on a String. Bad Job, Worse Uniform: Marina works as a hot dog vendor in the mall and has to wear a bucket full of weiners on her head. Navel Window: Marina shows off her bellybutton. Even Marina's work uniform shows this. Non-Mammalian Hair: She’s a fish with hair. Punny Name: Her name is a pun on "Maria" and it's a reference to the fact that as a sea creature, she is a "Marine" life form.

characters.name: Nocturna
characters.description: Pearl's friend, who is your typical goth girl. She works at a clothing store at the mall called Scorched Coral. Blank Stare: Her standard facial expression. Deadpan Snarker: Nocturna makes a lot of snarky sarcastic comments. Most of them are really dark and miserable. Goth: Nocturna is goth and, fittingly, she works at a Hot Topic-esque store in the Bikini Bottom Mall. Meaningful Name: "Nocturna" is derived from the word "Nocturnal", which relates to the night. The night is dark and Nocturna is dark.

characters.name: Nixie
characters.description: Cheery Pink: Nixie's bright and chipper personality is matched by her hair color, which is a very vibrant shade of hot pink. Genki Girl: Nixie is extremely happy all the time. Non-Mammalian Hair: A fish with hair. Pubescent Braces: One of Nixie's most notable physical traits is her large, flashy braces. Sweet Tooth: Nixie has a sweet brace-covered tooth when it comes to ice cream. In "The Goofy Newbie", she was a customer at Goofy Goober's Ice Cream Party Boat.

characters.name: Rube Goldfish
characters.description: Aperpetually-happytourist who mistook Patrick for a tour guide. Although he initially appeared to be an illusion created by the Tidal Zone, later episodes treat him like any ordinary fish. Ascended Extra: After appearing as the main character of "No Pictures Please", he becomes a recurring background character from Season 12 onwards, as well as beingSpongeBoband Patrick's tour guide to the surface world in "SpongeBob's Big Birthday Blowout". Big Fun: A sizable fish who's tons of fun to be around. Camera Fiend: Drives everyone crazy by constantly taking pictures of people. Catchphrase: "Amazing!"

characters.name: Dr. Gill Gilliam
characters.description: Bikini Bottom's resident doctor. Alliterative Name:GillGilliam, revealed in "Once Bitten". Back-Alley Doctor: Some episodes portray him as being incompetent at his job, such as "I Was a Teenage Gary", where he was "too squeamish" to inject Gary with snail plasma. A Lizard Named "Liz": A fish named Gill. New Job as the Plot Demands: Not only has he practiced in numerous fields of medicine, but he's also shown in one episode as a pirate.

characters.name: Lady Upturn CCCXXXIII
characters.description: A fancy rich lady, who thinks she's better than everyone else. Absurdly Long Limousine: Is shown to own one in "UpWard" which is many times the length of the Krusty Krab and takes several seconds for the entire thing to drive past the restaurant. Aesop Amnesia: In regards to her butler, Regigilled.Kamp Koral's "Regi-Hilled" centres around her firing him over some slightly cold tea, which causes a series of events that lead her to realise that she was wrong to do so and soon rehires him. However, later episodes like "Who's Complaining?" and "End of Summer Daze" shows that she still treats him poorly, explicitly prefering to give a parachute to a safe full of money instead of him.The Patrick Star Showand the main series continues this trend, showing that she hasn't changed a bit. Alliterative Name: Her original name,Ms.Mildred. Ascended Extra: After making a single appearance in Seasons 10 and 11, she started appearing a lot more often in the following seasons, even managing to be featured in bothKamp KoralandThe Patrick Star Show.

characters.name: Sticky Fins
characters.description: A criminal who escaped from prison and trickedSpongeBobinto thinking that he's his new driving instructor. Beard of Evil: He has a five-o-clock shadow and is a criminal. Final Boss: He and Dorsal Dan are the last antagonists of theKamp Koralspinoff. Non-Mammalian Hair: A fish with facial hair. Prefer Jail to the Protagonist: By the end of his debut episode, Sticky Fins begs the police to put him himself insolitary confinementjust to keepSpongeBobaway from him.

characters.name: Dorsal Dan
characters.description: A getaway driver and criminal. Alliterative Name:DorsalDan. The Bus Came Back: Returns in a speaking appearance in "Ain't That the Tooth" after being gone for about three seasons and only making silent cameos. Final Boss: He and Sticky Fins are the last antagonists of theKamp Koralspinoff. Getaway Driver: Dorsal Dan works as a getaway driver for Sticky Fins as he tries to arrive in time to help him escape.

characters.name: Helen the Felon
characters.description: A little girl with a criminal record. Beware the Cute Ones: She may be cute, but she's bad to the bone. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Helen looks and acts like a nice little girl but she's actually an evil villain, who's known for being Bikini Bottom's most wanted criminal. Enfant Terrible: Despite being a little girl, Helen has gotten herself sent to jail multiple times and for good reason too. She's wanted for various crimes of all sorts from assault to theft toselling girl scout cookies without a license. Even Evil Has Standards: In "Escape From Beneath Glove World", Helen says that she got arrested for murdering a guy. She follows this by admitting she was only joking and that her real reason for getting arrested was because she bit the guy running the lemonade stand.

characters.name: Captain / Painty the Pirate
characters.description: The painting of a pirate captain who appears in the show's opening. Alliterative Name:Painty thePirate. Ambiguous Situation: Whether or not he actually is Burger Beard fromThe SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Wateris left vague. The Cameo: While he appears in the intro for every episode, sometimes he appears in the episode proper. Examples include "Wet Painters" where he was one of the many paintingsSpongeBobhung on the wall to hide Mr. Krabs' ruined first dollar and in "Your Shoe's Untied" whereSpongeBobasks him how to tie his shoes and he tells him he cannot because he "be just a paintin' of a head." Insert Cameo: In an unusual example, his lips belong to the show's creator, Stephen Hillenburg.

characters.name: Hans
characters.description: A giant live-action hand. A Day in the Limelight: Hans is given a major role in "SpongeBob's Bad Habit", whereSpongeBobhas a nail-biting habit and goes to see a hypno-therapist to help him. Appropriately, this man in Hans and his hypnotism works like a charm. He also plays a big part in the episode "Handemonium", where he gets into a fight with the automated giant metal hand on top of the Chum Bucket. Depending on the Writer: Hans repeatedly switches from a right hand to a left hand throughout the series. This is most noticeable in "Handemonium", where he changes from a right to a left throughout the episode depending on what side of the screen he's coming from. Insert Cameo: The guy whose hand they took a picture of to play Hans is showrunner, Peter Bennett. Medium Blending: Hans is a live-action hand in an animated cartoon.

characters.name: Bubble Buddy
characters.description: A bubble-guy created bySpongeBobto be his buddy. Alliterative Name:BubbleBuddy. Ambiguous Situation:While there's no doubt he's alive at the end of his eponymous episode, it's not clear if he always was or if he came to life at some point. Animate Inanimate Object:At the end of his debut episode, it's revealed that he reallyisalive and presumably has been the whole time. Ascended Extra: He appears as one of the recurring companions inBattle for Bikini Bottom,often givingSpongeBobvaluable information on how to use abilities or defeat enemies, or just crack jokes with him.

characters.name: Man Ray
characters.description: Affably Evil: During his downtime, he's able to form actual friendships to the point he's happy to see one of his old high school friends again in "Shuffleboading". Ambiguously Human: He superficially resembles a man in some kind of costume, but when he takes his "mask" off, he appears to be headless. If "Man Ray Returns" andThe Patrick Star Showepisode "X Marks the Pot" are any indication,his body is fully human◊, but the question of what, if anything, is underneath his mask remains unresolved. Arch-Enemy: He's the main foe of Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy. Bad "Bad Acting": He literally says out loud "Oh sob! Oh cry!" when trying to act sad. Cool Mask: Subverted. What appears to be a helmetis actually his head, thoughhe can detach itand still is able to talk without it somehow.

characters.name: Dirty Bubble
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Object: He’s a sentient bubble. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Hadn't made a prominent appearance after "The Bad Guy Club for Villains" until the season 12 episode "Dirty Bubble Returns." Create Your Own Villain:The Patrick Star Showepisode "Super Sitters" revealed that Dirty Bubble was raised at the Super Child Daycare along with Mermaid Man, Barnacle Boy, Man Ray, and many others. When Patrick andSpongeBobtraveled back at this time, they showed him what he will destined to be as an adult along with Man Ray, The Coral Creep, and Exo-Woman. Final Boss: He’s the last antagonist faced in Season 1, only debuting at the end of the final episode. Good Costume Switch: When he's cleaned up and not mean.

characters.name: Atomic Flounder
characters.description: A flounder with radioactive powers, who is now retired. Grumpy Old Man: Atomic Flounder can be rather fussy, especially when he got ambushed bySpongeBob. I Was Quite a Looker: Despite being an old bag now, Atomic Flounder used to be a buff, muscular bodybuilder back when he was young and active.On the other hand, he had a single eye on his face, an arm growing from his right shoulder, and an eye growing from the right side of his head. Mutants: Atomic Flounder is the product of a radioactive disaster. Progressively Prettier:Zig-Zagged. His younger self was redesigned with a more muscular bodybuilder physique, unlike the standard flounder look the show uses. However, the redesign also made him more obviously mutated.

characters.name: Jumbo Shrimp
characters.description: Early Installment Character-Design Difference:His first appearance (while only on cardboard) has him looking like a muscular humanoid shrimp. His physical debut in "The Bad Guy Club For Villains" changes him drastically, looking more like a lobster. However, as of "Delivery of Doom", he's returned to his first design (althoughsmaller in size).After his redesign, he at first had a blue mask, which was later made green. His first appearance (while only on cardboard) has him looking like a muscular humanoid shrimp. His physical debut in "The Bad Guy Club For Villains" changes him drastically, looking more like a lobster. However, as of "Delivery of Doom", he's returned to his first design (althoughsmaller in size). After his redesign, he at first had a blue mask, which was later made green. Super-Powered Shrimp: Described as the most powerful of all crustaceans.

characters.name: Nosferatu
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: Needless to say, this version of Orlok isn't a murderous, plague-causing monster. Ascended Extra: He was a one-off gag in "Graveyard Shift", but became a recurring character in season 13. Dark Is Not Evil: Despite his creepy appearance, he's a very nice,if mischievous, guy. Deliberately Monochrome: He’s always depicted in black and white, a nod to the film he originates in. A Dog Named "Perro": Nosferatu is a term for vampire supposedly derived from the Romanian word for the creature.noteAlthough whether such a word ever actually existed is dubious.

characters.name: DoodleBob
characters.description: SpongeBoband Patrick's creation, a crude doodle ofSpongeBobcome to life, and on anUnstoppable Rage. Abusive Offspring: He's bothSpongeBoband Patrick's creation. Unfortunately, he holds no love for his creators and won't hesitate to erase them too. And I Must Scream: Inverted whenSpongeBobtrapped him in paper, making himGo Out with a Smile. However, this was howSpongeBobjustifiedDoodleBob'sUnstoppable Rage; He longed for a purpose that he could not fulfill as a crude drawing in a 3-dimensional world. Angry Eyebrows: Even provides the trope image! Once he's sufficiently angered, he draws a pair of these on his own face. Ax-Crazy: He seems to love random violence against others. When left to his own devices, he runs around babbling wildly, brandishing the giant pencil like a sword even when there's no one around.

characters.name: Baby Prunes / Mary's mother
characters.description: Abusive Parents: She constantly bosses Mary around. Ascended Extra: She returned to later seasons due to her popularity. Body Horror:It's revealed in herOrigins Episodethat her appearance is a result of being turned inside-out. Catchphrase: ABig "WHAT?!" A Day in the Limelight:Has her first major role in the Season 12 episode, "Biddy Sitting", whereSpongeBoband Patrick mistake her for a baby and "babysit" sit her for a day.Next would come "What Ever Happened to Baby Prunes?", serving as anOrigins Episodeabout her past career.

characters.name: SpongeTom
characters.description: Ascended Extra: He was only created for a one-off joke in "Broken Alarm" where Mr. Krabs was about to replaceSpongeBobfor being late. They later decided to make him a proper recurring character. Alliterative Name:SpongeTomShortPants. Catchphrase: “I’m prepared!” A Day in the Limelight: He's mostly only had minor appearances in several episodes, but the episode "Bizarro Bottom" is fully focused on his daily life. The episode also reveals that he lives in Tankini Top, a town that’s essentially aBizarro Universeof Bikini Bottom. Early Installment Character-Design Difference: Despite only appearing in three episodes so far, his character design changed enough between appearances to qualify. Specifically, his eyes were smaller and hadblack irises, his mouth was higher on his face and went off the sides of his head when he smiled, he had no dimples, and his bowtie was less detailed. His redesign in "Bizarro Bottom" seemed to be intended to make him look more likeSpongeBob.

characters.name: Narlene and Nobby
characters.description: Alliterative Family: They're siblings and their names both begin with the letter N. Alliterative Name: Both of their first and last names start with N. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: Narlene is pink and Nobby is yellow, neither of which are the color of actual narwhals. Animal Gender-Bender: Downplayed. Narlene has a tusk, and while female narwhals in real life can have them, only 15% of them do. Animals Not to Scale: Like Pearl, they are whales the size of fish.

characters.name: Roh and Rea
characters.description: Alliterative Family: They're brother and sister and their names both begin with R. Canon Immigrant: Like Narlene and Nobby, they made their debut in theKamp Koralspinoff, but were later featured as adults in the mainSpongeBobseries. Half-Identical Twins: They're twin siblings of different sexes, though while their physical appearances are distinct,their personalities aren't. Pink Girl, Blue Boy: Roh wears blue clothes and Rea is colored pink while wearing a purple dress. Rich Bitch: Much like their counselor Lady Upturn, they're wealthy and not very nice.

characters.name: Jimmy Blobfish
characters.description: Artistic License – Marine Biology: His appearance is based on a viral image of a blobfish… after decompressing from low pressure and dying. Real blobfish look different. Given that everyone in the Trawler cabin is to some degree morbid or undead, this may be deliberate. Canon Immigrant: He was originally created forKamp Koral, but subsequently made the transition to the mainSpongeBobseries, appearing as an adult in the episode "Kreepaway Kamp". Non-Mammalian Hair: As an adult in "Kreepaway Kamp," he has hair. Shout-Out: His adult self in the main series episode "Kreepaway Kamp" resembles Gomez Addams ofThe Addams Family, especially his mustache and haircut. Species Surname: His surname matches his species: Blobfish.

characters.name: Roxy
characters.description: Canon Immigrant: They originated inKamp Koral, but later appeared in the mainSpongeBobseries as adults in the episode "Kreepaway Kamp".
