Conjoined Twins: They're sisters connected to each other by virtue of Big Roxy being an anglerfish and Little Roxy being attached to her lure. Hair Substitute Feature: Big Roxy has a dorsal fin that takes the shape of hair. Irony: By the events of "Kreepaway Kamp", Big Roxy has become small while Little Roxy has become the larger conjoined twin. Pink Means Feminine: A pair of pink female twins.

characters.name: Preda Tory
characters.description: All Webbed Up: She's sometimes trapped other campers by wrapping them in her webbing. Artistic License – Marine Biology: She can spin webs like a spider, an ability that real sea spiders lack. Canon Immigrant: Like with every member of the Trawler cabin aside from Kidferatu (who is just a younger version of Nosferatu), she debuted inKamp Koraland subsequently appeared in the mainSpongeBobseries as an adult in the episode "Kreepaway Kamp". Projectile Webbing: Like a lot of spiders in fiction, she can shoot her webbing as a ranged weapon. Punny Name: Her name is a pun on "predatory".

characters.name: Regigilled
characters.description: Lady Upturn's butler. Canon Immigrant: He originated in theKamp Koralspinoff, but has since made appearances in the mainSpongeBobshow as well as in the other spinoffThe Patrick Star Show. A Day in the Limelight: His most prominent appearance is in theKamp Koralepisode "Regi-Hilled", where he moves in with Narlene and Nobby after Lady Upturn fires him for giving her tea that's two degrees too cold. Non-Standard Character Design: He's an octopus, but is notably one of the few octopus characters who looks nothing like Squidward. Punny Name: His name is an aquatic pun on the name Reginald.

characters.name: Elwood
characters.description: One of the campers at Kamp Koral. Butt-Monkey: He's often the victim of pranks and antics. Catchphrase: "This is fun!" Goofy Buck Teeth: A goofy side character with buck teeth. Hiding Behind Your Bangs: As a teen inThe Patrick Star Show, he has an edgy black hairstyle that covers one eye.

characters.name: Wise Kraken
characters.description: A giant kraken who likes to tell jokes. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: All he wears is a necktie. Canon Immigrant: He's another character originating fromKamp Koralwho also ended up making appearances inSpongeBoband is one of the few such characters to also be featured in the base show's other spinoffThe Patrick Star Show. Gag Nose: He's yet another character in the franchise with a bulbous nose, though that's to be expected from aRodney Dangerfieldcaricature. No Celebrities Were Harmed: His appearance and voice are based on comedianRodney Dangerfield.

characters.name: The Dartfish family
characters.description: A family of tiny dartfish who live in the Star household. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: An odd case where the cartoon version islessvividly colored. The Dartfish family are all blue, and some real dartfish are blue, but their distinct dorsal fins look most like those of thefire dartfish, which is a striking red and white in real life. Animal Facial Hair: Daddy Dartfish has a mustache. A Day in the Limelight: "Day of the Dartfish" focuses on the Dartfish family and Slappy, with Patrick only having a very minor role. Lilliputians: They’re extremely tiny, small enough to subsist on meals like a single peppermint candy.

characters.name: Captain Quasar
characters.description: A space captain shark from a cartoon. A Day in the Limelight: "Blorpsgiving" focuses entirely on him and Pat-Tron. Disembodied Eyebrows: Due to his eyes being on top of his head and his overall retro cartoon style, his eyebrows float above his eyes. Fish Out of Water: He plays this role during "Blorpsgiving" when he spends the holiday on Pat-Tron's planet with his family of robots. In Space, Everyone Can See Your Face: His space helmet is entirely transparent.

characters.name: Pat-Tron
characters.description: A Patrick-like robot who works for Captain Quasar. Alternate Species Counterpart: Pat-Tron is a robot version of Patrick, complete with a robot version of Patrick's family. Canon Immigrant: He appears in the main series episode "Welcome to Binary Bottom" after previously being exclusive toThe Patrick Star Show. A Day in the Limelight: "Blorpsgiving" focuses entirely on him and Captain Quasar. Disembodied Eyebrows: His eyebrows, which are zigzags like Patrick's, float above his eyes.

characters.name: Pat the Hapless
characters.description: AConan the Barbarian-style warrior Patrick. Animorphism: In "FitzPatrick," he gets turned into various animals by Beelzebass. Barbarian Longhair: A barbarian with long blond hair. Dumb Muscle: A brawny barbarian who's just about as stupid as Patrick. Inexplicably Identical Individuals: One of many characters inThe Patrick Star Showwho look like alternate universe Patricks.

characters.name: Beelzebass
characters.description: The evil wizard nemesis of Pat the Hapless. Animorphism: In "FitzPatrick," he uses spells to turn Pat the Hapless into various animals. Inexplicably Identical Individuals: He looks and sounds just like Bubble Bass. He may be his relative from another era. Losing Your Head: He's been beheaded by Pat the Hapless more than once, and keeps coming back. Nerd Glasses: Like Bubble Bass, he wears glasses and is a huge nerd.

characters.name: Dr. Plankenstein
characters.description: Cyclops: Much like Plankton, he’s aCyclopscopepod. Deliberately Monochrome: Designed in black and white. Dr. Fakenstein: Dr. Plankenstein is aMad Scientistversion ofPlankton. He's always seen in aDeliberately Monochromegothic castle, watching TV or scheming with his creationSpongeMonster(who looks likeSpongeBob) and bumbling assistant Patgor (who looks like Patrick). Inexplicably Identical Individuals: He looks and sounds a lot like Plankton, but it’s unclear if they’re related in any way. Mad Scientist: Natch, being a Victor FrankensteinExpy.

characters.name: Pat-gor
characters.description: Dr. Plankenstein's assistant. Deliberately Monochrome: Designed in black and white. Inexplicably Identical Individuals: Looks and sounds a lot like Patrick for no clear reason.

characters.name: SpongeMonster
characters.description: Dr. Plankenstein's monster. Deliberately Monochrome: Designed in black and white. Frankenstein's Monster: A play on this classic character resemblingSpongeBob. Inexplicably Identical Individuals: Looks like a giant monstrousSpongeBob.

characters.name: Slippy
characters.description: A female counterpart and love interest to Slappy. Distaff Counterpart: She's a female version of Slappy. The Flapper: She dresses like a flapper in "Tango Tangle". Look-Alike Lovers: She's a female version of Slappy and is implied to be in a relationship with him. Lorre Lookalike: Being a female counterpart to Slappy, she's aRare Female Exampleof aPeter Lorrecaricature.

characters.name: Clamu
characters.description: A non-anthropomorphic giant oyster at the Bikini Bottom Zoo, trained to perform tricks. Clamshells as Mouths: Her shell acts as a mouth. Loved by All: To the point where if anyone upsets or harms her in any way, they WILL feel the Bottomites’ wrath. Mama Bear:Do notsteal her egg. Punny Name: Her name is a pun onShamu.

characters.name: Hash Slinging Slasher
characters.description: Legend, or rather, Squidward, has it that a fry cook cut off his own hand with a spatula and was subsequently killed by a passing bus. Now his ghost haunts the Krusty Krab every Tuesday night with a vengeance. Little does Squidward know that there is more to his ghost story than he realized... or less, rather. Accidental Truth: Zig-zagged. Squidward told the made-up story of The Hash Slinging Slasher, only for all of these details of the story to start happening in real life, and then we're given one final rug pull, when "The Hash-Slinging Slasher"emerges from the shadowsandwe find out he's just a harmless nerdy dork named Richard. Artificial Limbs: The Hash Slinging Slasher replaced his severed arm with a spatula. Butt-Monkey: The Hash Slinging Slasher accidentally chopped his own limb off, got hit by a bus, and at his funeral, he was fired from his job.

characters.name: Janet and Marty
characters.description: Comically Missing the Point: WhenSpongeBobtries to reveal that he wasObfuscating Stupidityso they'd be impressed with Patrick looking smarter in comparison, they instead reach the conclusion that Patrick taughtSpongeBobto be more intelligent. Expy: OfMarge and Homer Simpson. Forgetful Jones: It takes until the end of the episode for them to remember that Patrick isn't their son and that they don't have a son in the first place. Non-Mammalian Hair: Janet has hair despite being a starfish. Spotting the Thread: Patrick figures out they're not his real parents when they address each other by their given names Janet and Marty (his real parents' names were later given as Herb and Margie, withThe Patrick Star Showlater retconning their given names as Cecil and Bunny).

characters.name: Alaskan Bull Worm
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Has made a couple of cameos in otherSpongeBobsource material, its most prominent appearance being inSpongeBob SquarePants: Creature from the Krusty Krabas the game's residentWomb Level. The Dreaded: One of the few legitimate examples in the series, being a monster worm capable of devouring anything. Extreme Omnivore: The Alaskan Bull Worm has an appetite for just about anything it comes across. This is taken to its logical extreme inSpongeBob SquarePants: Creature from the Krusty Krabwhere its bowels are littered with inedible junk that can't be digested. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: Due to their large size and predatory behavior, Alaskan Bull Worms appear to occupy a similar giant land predator niche to that of the extinct non-avian theropods. It Can Think: It's implied that the Alaskan Bull Worm isn't just a mindless creature, but a sentient being that destroys cities out of sheer malice.

characters.name: The Tattletale Strangler
characters.description: A feared serial killer in Bikini Bottom who has vowed to strangle anyone who dares turn him in to the police. Asshole Victim: If the Strangler wasn't established to be a violent criminal intending to killSpongeBob, all of the mental and physical tormentSpongeBobputs him through would be less funny. The Dreaded: He is feared far and wide throughout Bikini Bottom, even by Mr. Krabs, who was in the navy, and the huge, buff Larry. WhenSpongeBobtries to recruit a bodyguard at a local tough guy bar, all the patrons run away screaming in terror at the thought of challenging the Strangler. The police of Bikini Bottom are also unwilling to actively pursue him unless someone turns him in for them (though some of that is becausePolice Are Useless). Enraged by Idiocy: To the point he has a mental breakdown, and turns himself in just to escapeSpongeBob, whostillbelieves him to be his bodyguard even after he ripped off his mustache and revealed himself as the Strangler. Evil Laugh: He has an almighty one that he frequently busts out when he thinks he's going to get his way.

characters.name: Flats the Flounder
characters.description: A bully at Mrs. Puff's Boating School who wants to kickSpongeBob'sbutt. Abusive Offspring: At one pointSpongeBobtries to appeal to Flats's father for help, only for it to turn out he's also terrified of Flats as he's apparently kicked his butt in the past. Actor Allusion: He's the primary antagonist of the episode who's the threatening central bully toSpongeBob. He was also voiced byThomas F. Wilson, as he portrays a bullying character in theBack to the Futuremovies known as Biff Tannen, who's essentially anArch-Enemybully to MartyMcFly. Alliterative Name:Flats theFlounder. Ascended Extra: He was a background character for a few early episodes before coming into the spotlight as the infamous bully he's known as now.

characters.name: Mystery the Seahorse
characters.description: A seahorse whomSpongeBobbonds with, and causes hysteria for his job. Ascended Extra: She has a larger role in the Game Boy Advance port ofSpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom. Big Eater: She can eat almostanything, even things that aren't food. Extreme Omnivore: Not only does she eat the flowers thatSpongeBobplants and an entire Krusty Krab order, but also his employee hat, spatula, stove, and even Old Man Jenkins. She's a Man in Japan: Mystery is originally a female seahorse, but becomes a male in the Brazilian dub.

characters.name: Sea Bear
characters.description: A wild animal believed to be a hoax. Squidward accidentally summons one in an attempt to spiteSpongeBoband Patrick during their camping trip. Bears Are Bad News: Like actual bears, they are extremely dangerous if provoked, as Squidward could attest. Berserk Button: A variety of seemingly-minor things can summon/aggravate a sea bear (and subsequently a sea rhino), which include: playing the clarinet badly, waving a flashlight's light back and forth really fast, stomping the ground (as they take it as a challenge), eat cubed cheese (sliced is fine), wearing a sombrero in a goofy fashion, wearing clown shoes or a hula skirt, and screeching like a chimpanzee. If youdoend up facing off against a sea bear, attempting to escape will just prompt it to attack you more. The Bus Came Back: A Sea Bear returns in "Out of the Picture" and a few subsequent episodes afterwards. Real After All: Much to Squidward's horror, sea bears turn out to be real and not just myths.

characters.name: Sea Rhinoceros
characters.description: A wild animal that can be attracted by the sound of a sea bear attack. From Bad to Worse: Even if you get rid of the sea bear, now you have to deal with a sea rhino, which is impervious to the dirt circle that keeps sea bears away. Rhino Rampage: As they're probably even more dangerous than sea bears, this is a potentially likely outcome from attracting one. Weaksauce Weakness: Sea rhinos can be repelled if you wear anti-sea rhinoceros undergarments.

characters.name: SmittyWerbenJagerManJansen
characters.description: The skeleton of a dead fish, who was buried with a soda drinking hat.He was number one. Accidental Truth: Mr. Krabs makes up his name on the spot, when pressed about the original owner of the soda hat, but it turns out there really was a SmittyWerbenJagerManJansenwho owned the hat, died, and had it stolen from him. The Ace: While it's never stated what exactly Smitty did when he was alive, it was enough to have his tombstone shaped like a giant "#1", and he's apparently popular enough to have a whole army of zombies who would fight to help him retrieve his stolen soda drinking hat. Decapitation Presentation: Inverted, when he carried his own dismembered head when rising from the grave. Dem Bones: All that's left of him is a skeleton by the time Mr. Krabs unearths him, and he rises from the dead after his hat is stolen.

characters.name: Roger
characters.description: Mrs. Puff’s egg that hatches into a chick at the end of the episode. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Doesn’t return after his first appearance aside from a couple of video games (though one could argue that he technicallyreturnedin Season 14's "Friendiversary", if only for an unused animated design for him being repurposed for a brief gag). Companion Cube: His egg before he hatched into a chick. Conflict Killer: A non-fighting example. Roger is suddenly put in jeopardy whenSpongeBoband Patrick are fighting in detention and declaring their hate for each other, when the lamp keeping his egg warm suddenly goes out afterSpongeBobsayshe'd still hate Patrick if that exact thing happened, forcing the two quarrelling friends to make amends and work together to save the class mascot. Medium Blending: Roger in chick form is portrayed by two live-action stock footage clips of a chick (although it's worth noting thatthis originally wasn't going to be the case,as a model sheet exists for an animated design of Roger, withBlack Bead Eyes, a hairdo, and a sweater with his name on it; this design was eventually repurposed for "Friendiversary").

characters.name: The Gorilla
characters.description: Big Bad: Of the episode he appears in, and he is the one who manages to getSpongeBobto face his fear of going back outside aftera lucky recovery from breaking his butt. Half the Man He Used to Be: Rather than stuffing him in the bag like Patrick and Sandy, he splitsSpongeBobin half. It Can Think: At first he looks like a mindlessKiller Gorilla, untilSpongeBobquestions what a gorilla like like him is doing underwater, causing him to talk and freak out. Killer Gorilla: A violent gorilla that attacks both Patrick and Sandy ( and laterSpongeBob), though he doesn't kill any of them. Medium-Shift Gag: He’s played by a man in a gorilla suit.

characters.name: Carl
characters.description: Bad Boss: He'seven worsethan Mr. Krabs. He forces his employees to give "sincere service with a smile", and anyone who violates the rules gets beaten up by the burly men in Human Resources. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He may seem like aNice Guyat first, but it isn't long before he reveals howmorally bankrupthe is. Dissonant Serenity: It's quite eerie how utterly calm he is all the time, and he forces his employees to do the same. Evil Counterpart: To Mr. Krabs. While Krabs is grouchy, greedy, but has a soft spot he shows from time to time, and at least cares about serving real, delicious food to his clients, Carl is a seemingly friendly manager to the company that buys the Krusty Krab, but under his management, he's even more tyrannical towardsSpongeBoband Squidward, forcing the former to make synthetic Krabby Patties and the latter toput a front of perpetual hapliness under threat of physical harm. Faux Affably Evil: Carl isalways smilingandalways polite, even as he abuses his employees.

characters.name: Sergeant Roderick
characters.description: All There in the Script: His name is not mentioned in-episode, only in the credits. Artistic License – Military: He's stated to be a Sergeant, yet his jacket only has the markings of a Corporal (two chevrons instead of three). The Bus Came Back: After seemingly beingKilled Off for Real, he finally reappeared inSandy, Help Us!. Crippling Overspecialization: With his methods, Sergeant Roderick teachesSpongeBobto become an excellent driver, something Mrs. Puff herself couldn't accomplish... exceptSpongeBobcan only driveexactlyhow he was taught, which wasblindfolded. When Sarge informsSpongeBobit's illegal to drive with a blindfold in public and makes him remove it for the test,SpongeBobdoes disastrously, only managing to park the vehicle when he gets accidentally blinded. Didn't Think This Through: He forcesSpongeBobto learn how to drive while blindfolded. He actually succeeds, but fails to consider thatSpongeBobwouldn't know how to drive without a blindfold.

characters.name: Master Udon
characters.description: A con artist who tricksSpongeBobinto thinking that he's the "King of Karate". Actor Allusion: Master Udon is voiced byPat Morita, best known for his role inThe Karate Kid. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He at first appears as a nice sensei who's seemingly congratulatingSpongeBob. But he turns out to actually be a con artist as he tries to keepSpongeBobas a hostage so the latter and Sandy can buy a condo. The Cameo: Returns as a random wrestler in "Ma and Pa's Big Hurrah". Faux Horrific: Master Udon's true goal was to forceSpongeBobto buy into a timeshare, complete with a sales pitch. Downplayed as timeshares are a legitimate scam, though most timeshare salesmen rely on smooth-talking to convince the customer that it's a good idea instead of using force. When Udon presents his sales pitch,SpongeBobreacts in horror.

characters.name: Kelpy G
characters.description: A famous octopus renowned for his soothing clarinet performances. Ascended Extra: He was originally a mysterious man who was seen playing for the creatures that look suspiciously like Squidward's "Smelly" form at the end of "The Thing". He later became Squidward's main objective in "Smooth Jazz at Bikini Bottom", where he wants to listen to and meet him at one of his concerts. Jerkass to One: While he’s normally aNice Guyto everyone, he had no problem pushing Squidward to the floor when the latter was excitedly greeting himself (due to his bad clarinet playing). Mellow Fellow: He's unlike most other cephalopods seen in the show in that he's a pretty chill guy who likes to play soothing clarinet pieces. No Celebrities Were Harmed: He's a parody of saxophonist Kenny G.

characters.name: Jack M. Crazyfish
characters.description: The nemesis ofSpongeBob'sDream Sue, whoSpongeBobused as a scapegoat for his black eye until turns out he exists in real life, but in a more harmless fashion. Adaptational Wimp:SpongeBob's made-up stories have him progressively get weaker until he can be defeated with a novelty feather duster. Note that in the dream at the start of the episode,SpongeBobnever actuallywonthe fight. Ambiguous Situation: DidSpongeBobhear about Jack in passing to cause him to get worked into his dreams, or didSpongeBob's dreams coincidentally feature someone who turned out to be real? Big Eater: He comes to the Krusty Krab to order a custom Krabby Patty almost as big as his head. Dastardly Whiplash: His dream self plays this trope to a T, tying a woman to train tracks and twirling his mustache inSpongeBob's final made-up story. His real selfonly looks the part.

characters.name: Jim
characters.description: The first employee hired to be the fry cook at the Krusty Krab, now retired and rich after cooking for upscale restaurants. Actor Allusion: Possibly. Jim is an insanely good fry cook played by Patton Oswalt, much like Remy fromRatatouille, which came out around the same time as his debut episode. Always Someone Better: His skills as a fry cook are even greater thanSpongeBob's, and he was considered the "Best Employee Ever" by Mr. Krabs. According to Jim,SpongeBobis a good fry cook, but he can only become a great fry cook if he has the guts to leave the Krusty Krab. Big Brother Mentor:SpongeBobgrovels at Jim's feet to have him teach how to make better Krabby Patties. Jim complies, but beingThe Perfectionist,SpongeBobdoesn't achieve the result he's hoping for. Jim does think thatSpongeBobcould make it as a great fry cook if he were to leave the Krusty Krab. The Dog Bites Back: He was mistreated and underpaid by Mr. Krabs, so he left and caused the Krusty Krab to fall into disrepair. It's unclear if he knew the Krabby Patty Secret Formula, but if he did, he effectively achieved what Plankton had been targeting for years.

characters.name: Miss Gristlepuss
characters.description: Always Identical Twins: She has a large amount of identical sisters with varying colors. Fun-Hating Villain: She bans Krabby Patties not for any health code violations, but simply because they are described as fun and delicious. Genki Girl: Not anywhere close toSpongeBob's extent, but when she finally tried a Krabby Patty, she happily dances and sings the Krabby Patty song in the exact same waySpongeBobdid at the beginning of the episode. Happily Married: For what little is shown of them, she and Al seem to have a decent relationship. Heel–Face Turn: Upon trying a Krabby Patty herself, she decides not to arrestSpongeBoband Mr. Krabs when they sell them illegally in the former’s home, and unbanning the food.

characters.name: The Moth
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: To Mermaid Man. Pint-Sized Powerhouse: He's as small as Plankton but can lift up an entirelighthousebyhimself. Red Eyes, Take Warning: He's got red eyes and is a supervillain.

characters.name: The Warden
characters.description: The leader of Inferno Island, the prison islandSpongeBoband Patrick accidentally wind up at. Cool and Unusual Punishment: After learning about the kiddy stuff that happens at the summer campSpongeBobmeant to go to, he brings his inmates over to the camp as a punishment for their failed attempt at escaping. Drill Sergeant Nasty: Ermey seems to be having a blast as this character, giving himNO INDOOR VOICEand aLarge Hampersonality. Friendly Enemy:SpongeBoband Patrick treat him like he's the camp counselor and have no idea he's a tough as nails prison warden. Manly Tears: Sheds these duringSpongeBoband Patrick's play.

characters.name: T-119A, SPU-31, and Command Module
characters.description: Achilles' Power Cord: When combined, they consume so much power they need to be plugged in compared to their individual forms being able to operate without a cord. The extension cord is not long enough to reach the Krusty Krab, causing the combined robot to unplug itself and deactivate. Awesome, but Impractical: Their combined form gets rid oftheir inability to work togetherby giving Plankton full control and is capable of causing genuine destruction if Perch Perkin's news report is any indication. It alsorequires an extension cord, where SPU-31's weight causes causes the robot to topple over and smash all the components immediately after it loses power.And Command Module's windmill can hit Plankton to knock off his commander hat. Butt-Monkey: SPU-31 takes the most abuse out of the trio, breaking its top off on the doorway during its presentation to squirt all its liquid out, and getting beaten up by T-119A and Command Module while Plankton and Karen are arguing. Co-Dragons: What Plankton intended for them to be, feeling Karen wasn't actually helping him run the Chum Bucket or steal the Krabby Secret Formula and that he needed some alternatives. They fail spectacularly due to being poorly-constructed and unable to work together, whether asa teamorphysically combined. Combining Mecha: The three of them can combine to form a decently-sized robot, SPU-31, T-119A, and Command Module stacking onto each other in that order from bottom to top.

characters.name: Angry Jack
characters.description: A green, egg-shaped fish who owned a warehouse full of snail shells. An Arm and a Leg:SpongeBobwas too broke to pay for the damages, so Angry Jack makes him pay with an arm, leg, eyeball, and even organs. Mean Character, Nice Actor: His angry personality was originally just made for his commercials because according to him, “louder is the same as better”. NO INDOOR VOICE: He constantly shouts in his commercials. Rage Breaking Point: Even afterSpongeBobdestroys all of his inventory, he had yet to hit it untilSpongeBobmanaged to break the final shell which was claimed to be indestructible.SpongeBob:Are you really angry or are you just trying to sound louder?Angry Jack:I’M REALLY ANGRY!!Announcer:Blistering fury!

characters.name: Queen Amphitrite
characters.description: Abusive Parents:Downplayedbut still shown. She does nothing to stop King Neptune from imprisoning Triton and tries to make him forget about the incident rather than helping him solve it. Ancient Grome: She is actually the wife of Posideon in Greek mythology, while Salacia is the wife of Neptune in Roman mythology. Commuting on a Bus: She makes a short cameo in "Trident Trouble", but other than that does not reappear prominently after her debut. Jerkass Gods: Much like her husband, Amphitrite will abuse her powers when provoked and is not a pleasant person in general,especially to Mr. Krabs. Out of Focus: She has no involvement in the conflict between Neptune and Triton, and doesn't even appear in the movie Neptune made either.

characters.name: Triton
characters.description: Deadpan Snarker: He becomes this as he grows locked away in the cage. Green and Mean: He has green skin like his father and becomes him afterSpongeBoband Patrick free him from his cage. Karma Houdini: He gets no comeuppance at all for the destruction he caused on Bikini Bottom. Instead, he'spraisedfor it. Punished for Sympathy: Triton creates a cure for diseases, but Neptune shuns him for it because as Gods, they don't care about diseases nor do they get them. Put on a Bus: He does not appear after his debut episode.

characters.name: Puffy Fluffy
characters.description: A vicious animal whomSpongeBobnaively bought for Gary so he could have a playmate to keep him company, andSpongeBobthinks Gary is ignoring him whenever he attacks him when not present. In reality, despite his seemingly harmless appearance, he, along with other members of his species, is extremely dangerous and hostile toward other pets, especially snails. Beneath the Mask: Don't trust his cute appearance one bit. He is a dangerous monster who intends on eating Gary. Berserk Button:Don't you everput him in a house with another pet. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: At a first glance, he seems like an adorable, innocent little creature, but once exposed to another pet (sea snails especially), all hell will break loose. Cartoon Creature: He resembles a blowfish, piranha, or angler fish in cute form, while his monster form resembles more of an eel. His species was in fact unnamed throughout the episode, though certain source releases call him a "nudibranch" (a type of sea slug).

characters.name: Karen  2
characters.description: And There Was Much Rejoicing: After the crowd at the Krusty Krab expresses shock at Karen 2 accidentally running over Plankton, the original Karen killing her replacement in response toher lack of concern over her husband's injuriesearns Karen 1 cheers from said crowd. Armless Biped: Unlike the original Karen, she wasn't built with arms, something she snarks at Plankton about when she's struggling to get through the Krusty Krab's front door. Awesome, but Impractical: Plankton brags she has triple the processing power of the original Karen, "all the latest software, and a sleek space-age design." In execution, she can't even open doors by herself due to not being built with arms, and her compartment to carry Plankton is at the bottom of her "dress" when she has the flexibility to kick as high as her own head to cause him to fall out and right underneath her, accidentally crushing him in the process. Even if she wasn't destroyed in response to showing she lacks any of her predecessor's love for her husband, it's apparent Plankton would have either rushed back to his old wife or built a Karen 3 due to Karen 2's poor performance. Deader than Dead: First Karen 1 smashes her pieces, next Plankton removes the battery powering Karen 2 to transfer to his ex-wife after she ran out of power, then Karen 2's remainssuddenly explode, and finallySpongeBobsuggests rebuilding Karen 2 only for Mr. Krabs to instead use what's left of her as a cheap robot costume for Squidward to wear. Deadpan Snarker: She shares the same penchant for snark as her original counterpart, with both of them snarking at each other and her snarking at Plankton for not giving her arms.

characters.name: Shiny Bubble
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Matter: Like his father, he's a living soap bubble. Came Back Wrong: When Shiny pops,SpongeBobtries to blow him back and reshape him but ends up shaping him into a monster and then a dinosaur. Once he finally gets it right, a second head appears. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He does not return in any other episode after his debut, nor in “Bubbletown” despite Bubble Buddy appearing. Karma Houdini: He gets no punishment for his recklessness in Bikini Bottom. Kids Are Cruel: He is a bubble portrayed as a young boy who causes destruction in Bikini Bottom. At the end, he blows a raspberry atSpongeBob.

characters.name: Kenny the Cat
characters.description: A cat who's famous in the underwater realm for being able to hold his breath for a very long time.SpongeBobis a huge fan of him and is delighted when he comes to visit Bikini Bottom. Alliterative Name:Kenny theCat. Animals Not to Scale: He’s taller than many of the sea creatures, but not by much. A real adult cat would dwarf most of the main characters, but he barely stands out. Broken Pedestal:SpongeBobdiscovers that Kenny secretly uses an oxygen tank hidden in his fur to regain his breath. Kenny manages to convinceSpongeBobto keep it a secret, but his cover is blown after Sandy calls his bluff and pressures him to explain how he's managed to hold his breath for so long. I Just Want to Be Special: Kenny wants to be famous underwater because on the surface, there's nothing remarkable about him.SpongeBobsuggests he could be famous just for being a mammal that lives underwater, similar to Sandy, though she shuts it down by sending Kenny home right then and there.

characters.name: Cuddle E. Hugs
characters.description: Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: He wears only a top hat and a bowtie. All Just a Dream:He's revealed at the end of the episode to be a real-life hamster who dreamed of being in Bikini Bottom due to his owner's love ofSpongeBob. Dream Sue: His unusual powers are all due to himbeing the dream of a real-life hamster. I'm a Humanitarian: He eats a large number of Bikini Bottom residents. Meaningful Name: He loves to cuddle and give hugs. Additionally, his middle name, eventually revealed to be Eat, represents his desire to eat people.

characters.name: Tony
characters.description: Bigger on the Inside: Tony's shell comes with a bed, a kitchen, a bathroom, and a home gym. Informed Species: Tony lacks the streamlined shell and flippers that sea turtles have in real life. Instead, he has a domed shell and legs that make him resemble a tortoise or box turtle. No Such Thing as Drowning: Exaggerated. He was apparently sleeping on the ocean floor for three decades without having to breathe on the surface. Non-Mammalian Hair: A turtle with hair on his head, brows, and chest. Rambunctious Italian: He speaks and acts like a stereotypical Italian-American.

characters.name: Notodoris
characters.description: All There in the Script: Her name is never said aloud in her debut episode, only appearing in the credits. Angry Eyebrows: She has a pair of them atop her eyestalks. Artistic License – Marine Biology: She’s supposedly a sea slug, but she has eyestalks like a land slug. A Dog Named "Dog":Notodorisis a real genus of nudibranchs (sea slugs) that includes multiple yellow species, so Notodoris is most likely actually an actual notodoris slug. Eye on a Stalk: She has eyestalks (unlike real sea slugs).

characters.name: Suzie Groove
characters.description: Even the Girls Want Her: Notably, Karen took a lot of interest in watching her sway her hips. Goofy Buck Teeth: She has big teeth. Hartman Hips: Her most prominent feature, which she likes to show off a lot. Lascivious Beauty Mark: She has a white mole on her face. Parent Service: She stands out for being one of the more attractive characters in the show due to her wide hips.

characters.name: Octward
characters.description: A squid who works as a cashier at the Krunchy Krab, a restaurant inTankini Topthat serves tacos. A Dog Named "Cat": A trait he shares withhis Bikini Bottom counterpart. Squidward is actually an octopus, while Octward is actually a squid. Evil Counterpart:Inverted. While Squidward is more of aJerkassthan outright evil, Octward is an actualNice Guy. Friendly Shopkeeper: In contrast to his Bikini Bottom counterpart, who serves as the page image forApathetic Clerkand is usually annoyed bySpongeBob, Octward is one of these, who is happy to seeSpongeTom. Mondegreen Gag: When he introduces himself toSpongeBob,SpongeBobmishears his name as "awkward" and says that what's happening is awkward (as he's never been to Tankini Top before, and only accidentally went there since he was sleeping on the bus and missed his stop in Bikini Bottom).

characters.name: Mr. Claws
characters.description: A crab who works as the manager of the Krunchy Krab, a restaurant inTankini Topthat serves tacos. Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: He's a blue crab. Benevolent Boss: In contrast tohis Bikini Bottom counterpart, who isgenerallyagreedyBad Boss, Mr. Claws is one of these. He not only letsSpongeTomleave early, but also gives him a day off. Even at his most generous, Mr. Krabs would never letSpongeBobhave so much time off. Evil Counterpart:Inverted. Mr. Krabs isn't evil, but heisaBad Bosswho can be aJerkassto his employees at times. By comparison, Mr. Claws is a much nicer boss, and is kind to his employees.

characters.name: Squidmund
characters.description: Birds of a Feather: WithSpongeBoband Patrick. Fun Personified: He's very chipper and fun loving, and thinks Squidward is a "fuddy duddy stick-in-the-muddy".

characters.name: The Kraken
characters.description: Attention Whore: He's implied to be this, since his real concern was less of being solitary and more because people didn't look at him as just as important as the other circus personalities. Bond Villain Stupidity:Just as he's about to eat the Bikini Bottom population, he decides to grant Pearl a final wish to sing a song as they await their doom. He failed to realize it was a trap by Mr. Krabs to shatter the glass jar they were all trapped in, causing the Kraken's entire scheme to unravel and for him to beflicked away to parts unknown. Canon Foreigner: He is exclusive toSpongeBob Comicsand doesn't appear in any otherSpongeBobmedia. Evil Is Petty: He has no justifiable reason to devour all sea life in Bikini Bottom other thanpeople not noticing him, which is hardly a sympathetic excuse to begin with. Faux Affably Evil: He tries to sound cordial toSpongeBoband the gang, but they see through that facade quickly.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Demoted to Extra: Zig-zagged, some of them, such as Tom, Don The Whale, Sandals, Harold, Nat Peterson, Norma Rechid, Nancy, Evelyn, Jimmy Gus, and Scooter were more prominent in the first three seasons, but then quickly froze into the background, while others, such as Frankie Billy and Mimi quickly became far more important as the series goes on although they lost prominence since Season 9. Depending on the Writer: Because of their roles as background characters to be used for quick gags, they don't really have consistent personalities, voices, ages or even genders, at least at first. A lot of them got more consistent personalities as the seasons went on with Fred being major example. Didn't Think This Through: All of them have their moments of impulsivity. Fatal Flaw: All of them have one, but just about every member showed signs of impulsiveness and hostility towards the others. Hypocrite: Most of them are this. An example includes Harold getting offended at Mr. Krabs’ underwear even though he was naked (and seemingly lots of fish are naked despite the main characters getting arrested for it).

characters.name: Tom (Incidental 6)
characters.description: A large olive-green fish withanger issueswho is well known for saying "CHOCOLATE!" Ax-Crazy: Even before the "CHOCOLATE" incident, there were a few instances where he was pretty terrifying.WhenSpongeBobsays "April Fools" when he gives him back his drink, he grabsSpongeBobby the shirt and screams, demanding to know what he's done.When Bubble Buddy first was in Bikini Bottom and wreaked havoc, he piped up with this exchange.Tom:He poisoned our water supply, burned our crops, and delivered a plague unto our houses!!!Townspeople:He DID?!?Tom:No!But are we gonna wait around until he does?!? WhenSpongeBobsays "April Fools" when he gives him back his drink, he grabsSpongeBobby the shirt and screams, demanding to know what he's done. When Bubble Buddy first was in Bikini Bottom and wreaked havoc, he piped up with this exchange.Tom:He poisoned our water supply, burned our crops, and delivered a plague unto our houses!!!Townspeople:He DID?!?Tom:No!But are we gonna wait around until he does?!? Comedic Sociopath: He qualifies to some extent, given how unpredictably hostile he can be.

characters.name: Scooter (Incidental 38)
characters.description: A purple surfer fish who appears mostly in the background, but has some major roles. Beware the Nice Ones: He is indeed friendly, but sometimes joins the riot with the other incidental characters. Demoted to Extra: He was more prominent in the first three seasons, but then became demoted to more non-speaking roles. Dropped a Bridge on Him: Subverted. He appears to be killed off in a contrived manner when he drowns in "Bubble Buddy", but he comes back in later episodes alive and well. Unless he's a ghost and Nickelodeon'sBikini Bottom Mysteriesepisode on him can be taken with some degree of canon. Everyone Has Standards: He was just as offended as everyone else bySpongeBobpretending to drown in "Ripped Pants", and can only muster up a solemn "Dude..." to express his disappointment in him afterwards.

characters.name: Nat Peterson (Incidental 41)
characters.description: Borrowed Catchphrase: In "Squid Baby", Nat steals Fred's "My Leg!" catchphrase, in a rather witty and subversive manner.Nat:[horrified]MY FACE! MY FACE![flatly]Also my leg,[horrified]BUT MOSTLY MY FACE!!! Continuity Drift: Nat's name has changed from episode to episode, often being "Tucker" or "Peterson" (as his first name). However, the Bikini Bottom Mysteries episode, titled him "Nat Peterson", making this the closest we have to an official name. A Day in the Limelight: The episode "Plankton's Regular" was all about Nat becoming a regular customer at The Chum Bucket. The episode's climax revealed, however, that he wasn't going regularly- Karen was actually paying him to do, and after he can stomach no more chum, he gives up on the deal. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Nat’s just as hostile and antagonistic as any other incidental most of the time, but he’s willing to be friendly and pleasant on a few occasions. Mellow Fellow: Generally pretty chill & laid-back, but like the other background characters, he isn't someone to forget to join the riot.

characters.name: Harold (Incidental 40)
characters.description: Early Installment Character-Design Difference: In the first season and parts of the second season (before character models were revised), he was typically completely naked. Flanderization: In the first season, Harold started off as a character who only got angry if things didn’t go his way, however, as of the second season, he gets angry over quite everything! Given Name Reveal: His name was revealed in "Roller Cowards". Hair-Trigger Temper: Similar to Tom, he's frequently depicted as quick to anger. I Have Many Names: As demonstrated above, his name is never consistent across the series.

characters.name: Sandals (Incidental 156)
characters.description: The Ditz: Sandals is definitely not the sharpest tool in the shed, somewhat justified because almost all characters on the show are stupid. Everyone Has Standards: He’s disturbed bySpongeBob’sblack eye inBlackened Sponge. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He generally joins the riot of other incidentals, but isn't really a bad person. Kick the Dog: Sandals gives a speech toSpongeBobinStuck in the Wringerafter witnessing the former blow up (figuratively speaking) at Patrick with no context. This leads to him essentially tellingSpongeBobhe’s rotten to his very core. Kindhearted Simpleton: Not so much of a smart character, but still pretty amiable most of the time.

characters.name: Norma Rechid (Incidental 49)
characters.description: Beware the Nice Ones: She, along with Scooter, is one of the nicer incidental characters, but she sometimes joins the riot with the other incidental characters. Gag Lips: Norma has big red lips on her at nearly all times. Good Parents: On the occasion that she’s portrayed with kids, she’s normally shown to be kind towards them. Hospital Hottie: Perhaps not "hottie", butshe is quite cute, and has been portrayed as a friendly nurse (or a sardonic one). Interspecies Romance: Norma is a pipefish, and is married toDoodleBob, a doodle ofSpongeBob.

characters.name: Suzy Fish (Incidental 7)
characters.description: Deadpan Snarker: WhenSpongeBobasks her which order his pencils should go in, she responds with "I think it goes stuck inside your-" before beingcut off bySpongeBob. InBand Geeks, she referred toSpongeBobas talking cheese in a rather disparaging tone. Jerkass: She is usually portrayed as an unpleasant and easily triggerable character, similar to Harold. In "Tunnel of Glove", she makes fun of Pearl by callingSpongeBobhis boyfriend throughout the episode. Vague Age: Some appearances have her portrayed as a teenage friend of Pearl, others portray her as a mother with kids.

characters.name: Janet (Incidental  49 A)
characters.description: The Inspector Is Coming: Her debut involves her visiting Squidward’s house to see if she can sell it, kicking off the plot. Screw This, I'm Out of Here!: Following her mounting frustration at Spongebob, Patrick, Squidward, and even ‘’Gary’’ calling themselves “Squidward”, Janet storms off and refuses to sell Squidward’s house.

characters.name: Mermaid Man
characters.description: SpongeBoband Patrick's favorite superhero, who is now elderly and lives in a retirement home. His real name is Ernie Huckler. Acrofatic: Despite putting on more and more weight due to his retirement, and also being very old, he still has the same agility as he had when he and Barnacle Boy were active superheroes. Alliterative Name:MermaidMan. Ambiguously Human: He certainlylookshuman—at least, about as much like a human as you can get in the show's standard artstyle—but nearly all other humans in the series are depicted viaMedium Blendingand are shown to be far larger than the main cast, neither of which is true for him and Barnacle Boy. He doesn't look like the Atlanteans we've seen in the series, either. The character he's inspired by is most often half-human, half-Atlantean, but Mermaid Man himself has no clear origin story, which makes his true nature rather uncertain. Eventually, the show clarifies that he and Barnacle Boyarehuman. In Mermaid Man's case, he just needs a magical starfish to breathe underwater. Artificial Gill: Mermaid Man's magical starfish, which he always wears over his nose. InMermaid Man Begins, a wave took him and he was sucked into the ocean floor, but he was rescued by mermaids and given the starfish so he could breathe underwater.

characters.name: Barnacle Boy
characters.description: Mermaid Man's sidekick, who is also elderly and lives in the same retirement home. His real name is Tim StanglernoteIn "Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy V",his first name is Kyle. Alliterative Name:BarnacleBoy. Ambiguously Human: Like his mentor, he doesn't match up with the other humans in the series, nor the Atlanteans, and he doesn't have any real origin story, making it hard to definitively say what he is. "Mermaid Man Begins" clarifies that he is indeed human. Atrocious Alias: Given that he lives in an underwater society where the word "barnacle" is sometimes used as an expletive, it's likely a factor as to why he's treated with less respect than Mermaid Man. Butt-Monkey: He is the main target of the show's slapstick comedy in the episodes he appears in. In "Mermaidman & Barnacleboy II", him being set on fire by the pipes of Mermaid Man's boatmobile is aRunning Gag, with the Dirty Bubble even implying that he regularly suffered said injury even when the two heroes were younger.

characters.name: Mindy
characters.description: A friendly mermaid who does her best to assistSpongeBoband Patrick in their quest to Shell City. She disproves of her father's method of ruling with an iron fist, and wishes he would use a little love and compassion. She is also the target of Patrick's affections. Amazing Technicolor Population: She and her father have green skin. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: Her shirt is small enough to expose her belly button. Her feminine trait is primarily that she is caring, as she is aware of her father's tyranny and wishes he would rule with compassion instead of anger. Bespectacled Cutie: She's a cute bespectacled girl with a sweet personality. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl: Mindy's aNice Girland King Neptune is aJerkass God.

characters.name: Dennis
characters.description: A hitman hired by Plankton to make sure thatSpongeBoband Patrick never make it to Shell City. He is a living example of the movie'sDarker and Edgiertone. Adaptation Dye-Job:Some of the media surrounding his appearance in the movie alter the color of his clothes a bit. In the console video game and certain toys, he wears blue jeans instead of black leather pants and a white shirt instead of a gray shirt. Those appearances also give him a unique black ponytail underneath the hat too which also is present in theRoad Trip in 3-Dpicture book based on the movie.HisCameoin the show proper retain alterations like the grey shirt and blue jeans while also further recoloring his black shades to blue and his black cowboy hat to brown. Overall, he has aa brighter appearance more suitable for the lighter toneof the show. Some of the media surrounding his appearance in the movie alter the color of his clothes a bit. In the console video game and certain toys, he wears blue jeans instead of black leather pants and a white shirt instead of a gray shirt. Those appearances also give him a unique black ponytail underneath the hat too which also is present in theRoad Trip in 3-Dpicture book based on the movie. HisCameoin the show proper retain alterations like the grey shirt and blue jeans while also further recoloring his black shades to blue and his black cowboy hat to brown. Overall, he has aa brighter appearance more suitable for the lighter toneof the show. Always a Bigger Fish:Gets stomped on by the Cyclops when he himself was about to stomp onSpongeBoband Patrick. Subverted as he survives this and comes back a few scenes later.

characters.name: Victor
characters.description: The owner of the Thug Tug. His bar's most "important" rule is "all bubble-blowing babies will be beaten senseless by every able-bodied patron in the bar". Abhorrent Alpha Male: He's your average tough guy with a pathetic sense of masculinity. Heck, even his bar's most "important" rule is to simplynotblow bubbles, which already sounds weak in and of its own. All There in the Script: Only named in the credits. Asshole Victim: Considering he made a rule against blowing bubbles and that whoever does gets beaten senseless, no one really feels anything for him when he tries to enforce this on Dennis, only to learn the hard way that Dennis isn't someone you wanna mess with. Bad Guy Bar: He's the owner of the Thug Tug, a bar where all sorts of crooks and hooligans hang out.

characters.name: The Cyclops
characters.description: The guardian of Shell City, who is actually a man in a diver suit that he never takes off. 24-Hour Armor: It seems he never takes his diving gear off, not even when he’s on dry land. Always a Bigger Fish: StompsDenniswhen he is first introduced. Bad People Abuse Animals: Not only are all his souvenirs made of real sea creatures, but he alsolaughs maniacally as he kills them. It's implied that he knows the fish he kills are sentient, andfinds their suffering amusing. Creepy Old-Fashioned Diving Suit: He is only ever seen wearing a bulky deep-sea diver suit with a green glow coming from its helmet, adding to his mysteriousness.

characters.name: David Hasselhoff
characters.description: Adam Westing: This version of David Hasselhoff is a super-powered lifeguard who cruises through the water like a speedboat and has a launch pad inside his pecs. Amusing Injuries: He gets burned by fire from King Neptune's trident shortly after sendingSpongeBoband Patrick to the Krusty Krab. All that happens to him is that hegets covered in ashand says "Ow". As Himself: One of history's most delightfully inexplicable examples of celebrities playing themselves. The Bus Came Back: 15 years after the release of the movie, he reappeared for a few short appearances inSpongeBob'sBig Birthday Blowout. Celebrity Power: Has a mysterious set of superpowers which can't really be explained by anything other than the fact that he's David Hasselhoff.

characters.name: King Neptune's Squire
characters.description: King Neptune's Squire, who accompanies Neptune pretty much wherever he goes, and must obey his every command. Butt-Monkey: Gets hit over the head by Neptune twice. Only Known by Their Nickname: He is only addressed as "squire" throughout the movie. What Happened to the Mouse?: He disappears from the movie whenSpongeBoband Patrick return to the Krusty Krab 2, with no answer as to whether he ended up being enslaved by Plankton as well or not.

characters.name: Floyd and Lloyd
characters.description: Two hillbillies who work the gas station at the edge of the county line. All There in the Script: Floyd is only named in the credits. Bullying a Dragon: They're dumb enough to make fun ofDennis, and they are rewarded with getting their mouths promptly ripped off. Everyone Has Standards: Though they made fun of Bob and Pat for their determination to go to Shell City, after the heroic duo laughs back at them andpress on anywaysdespite being rid of their Patty Wagon, Floyd and Lloyd start to worry a bit about them as the duo walk away.Floyd:...they're dead. Hate Sink: There’s not much to like about these two despite them not being outright villains, so you won’t feel too sorry for them when they bite off more than they can chew after antagonizing Dennis.

characters.name: Burger-Beard the Pirate
characters.description: The main antagonist ofThe SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water, a pirate who seeks the Krabby Patty secret formula. Affably Evil: Despite being a thief, he refuses to hurt innocent civilians to the point where he politely tells them to move out of the way while he is driving. Burger-Beard is also willing to sing theSpongeBobSquarePantstheme song with his seagull crew. Badass Normal: Manages to put up a winning battle againstSpongeBoband his friends after they gain superpowers while being just an ordinary human. Big Bad: OfSponge Out of Water. Canon Character All Along: Implied. It's revealed with the paint-over before the rap battle started that he is or the model used for Painty the Pirate, the intro singer.

characters.name: Bubbles the Dolphin
characters.description: And I Must Scream: He reveals that he hated his job asThe Watcherfor this reason, as he had been bound by duty to watch the cosmos for eons. Fluffy the Terrible: His name is rather silly and while he doesn't look terrifying he has immense powers and can shoot lasers from his blowhole. Head Blast: Bubbles can fire laser beams from the blowhole on his head. Heel–Face Turn: Goes from trying to killSpongeBobto helping him. Heroic Dolphin: Gives the main characters the ability to breathe air.

characters.name: King Poseidon
characters.description: The main antagonist ofThe SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run. 0% Approval Rating: It turns outeveryone in Atlantic City dislikes him, including his own administrator (whose been a long-sufferingBeleaguered Assistant), and that his subjects only pretended to like him because they were afraid of his power. Bad People Abuse Animals: Captures snails and uses their slime as facial cream. Once they run out he makes them work as slaves. Balloon Belly:It turns out he's actually fat, but was hiding his gut with a golden plate. Big Bad: OfSponge on the Run.

characters.name: Otto
characters.description: A robot that Sandy invented and gave to Mr. Krabs. Later discarded and adopted by Plankton and Karen who use him to driveSpongeBobto Atlantic City. Ambiguous Gender: Appears to be a male robot based on the masculine name and being referred to as "he" by Sandy. Although, some characters also use "it" to refer to Otto, and Otto is also played by a woman and speaks with a noticeably femininenote(albeit raspy, it being voiced by Awkwafina and all)voice. As a robot, Otto might just simply not have a gender. Catchphrase: "You're fired." Often said at inopportune times due to being programmed by Sandy as a managerial personality. Happily Adopted: After being fired for being too good at it's job by Mr. Krabs, it got "adopted" by Plankton and Karen, who she sees it as a sort of son to her. The Gambling Addict: Is revealed to have become this after spending too much time in Atlantic City.

characters.name: Sage
characters.description: A mystical sagebush who givesSpongeBobadvice. A Dog Named "Dog": He's a sage made of sagebrush named Sage. Big Good: He's the most powerful force in the movie who aidsSpongeBoband Patrick in saving Gary. Only Sane Man: Is an adult having to intervene in the childish duo ofSpongeBoband Patrick misinterpreting his instructions about the Sage Coin or getting distracted by the fantastic luxuries and entertainment in Atlantic City. After the two gamble away the coin, Sage walks out fed up with them screwing up the mission to save Gary. So Proud of You: Though he does returns at the end to praiseSpongeBobfor being able to retrieve Gary and force Poseidon to have a change-of-heart.

characters.name: El Diablo
characters.description: A fearful gunman in a Western town who Sage claims is controlling the zombies souls. The Dreaded: He getsverylittle description other than being this. Filler Villain: Sorta, he basically exists to make the trip harder for the series and being pretty unconnected to the plot. As the above trope shows there's not much known about him or to talk about. The Irredeemable Exception: Played with, he's the only one of the villains of the movie to die. Killed Off for Real: Yeah, pretty much after being incinerated. SeeNot Quite Deadfor more.

characters.name: Sparky
characters.description: Half the Man He Used to Be: He loses his back half when Bikini Bottom gets lifted off the sea floor. Mechanical Horse: He acts very much like a normal horse (down to making snorting noises) in spite of being a robot. Out of Focus: When Sandy andSpongeBobset off to find their friends, Sparky (at least his upper half) is left behind, not appearing again until the end of the film. His back half participates in getting Bikini Bottom out of the lab, but doesn't get much more significance.

characters.name: Sue Nahmee
characters.description: A CEO who runs the B.O.O.T.S laboratory. Animal Motifs: Her whole life revolves around fish and the ocean; her nameis a punon "tsunami", her blue hair resembles waves, she named her dog Cuda (after barracuda),and she winds up becoming a fish by the end. Bad Boss: She treats her two employees Phoebe and Kyle like trash, bribing them with the false promise of a fully stocked vending machine (and paying for said vending machine with their paychecks). Bad People Abuse Animals: Her plot involves cloning sea creatures at the cost of essentially killing the original. On a minor scale, she also lets her mutant fish kiss her dog, who is clearly terrified of it. Big Bad: OfSaving Bikini Bottom.

characters.name: Cuda
characters.description: Dogs Hate Squirrels: Chases Sandy andSpongeBobaround the B.O.O.T.S. Waterpark during the third act of the film. A Dog Named "Cat": A pug whose name is the latter half of "barracuda", keeping with his owner's love of fish. Jealous Pet: Implied to be this with his owner's mutant fish, along with fearing the creature when being forced to let it kiss him. Heel–Face Turn: Possibly for reasons stated above, he plays a role in freeing the Bikini Bottomites. He is even later shown attending the Cheeks Family circus along with the other scientists. Mister Muffykins: The lap dog of Sue Nahmee.

characters.name: Phoebe and Kyle
characters.description: Heel–Face Turn: They eventually decide to stop following Sue Nahmee's orders and help Sandy and the others return home. An Odd Place to Sleep: Kyle sleeps in a cabinet drawer (filed under K), and basically lives in the lab without Sue's knowledge. Punch-Clock Villain: While they contribute to the main villain's plot, they are really a pair of goofballs that she walks all over. Tiny Guy, Huge Girl: Played with. At the end of the film, Sandy has used her shrink ray on them so they could attend the circus with her family and the Bikini Bottom residents. Kyle wonders why Phoebe is still bigger than him.

characters.name: The Rattlesnakes
characters.description: All There in the Script: With the exception of Bonnie, their individual names are only given in the end credits. Fur Is Clothing: After being squeezed out of their skins, they are shown wearing pajamas or underwear underneath. Yet they still leave inembarrassment of being apparently naked. Non-Mammalian Hair: The snake leader Butch has a big dark mustache on his face. The Smurfette Principle: Bonnie is the only female rattlesnake in the group, which is especially noticeable when she is left in her underwear, as her undergarments are frilly and feminine in contrast to her four male cohorts wearing boxer shorts or long underwear. Snakes Are Sinister: A gang ofWestern Rattlerswho make their arrival in a big ol' cowboy boot and attack the main heroes.

characters.name: Hydra Karens
characters.description: Animal Motifs: They resemble the real-life hydras that live in the sea, which are not dragons or snakes but are marine invertebrates that reproduce by budding. Just like them, Karen "splits" into the three (later four) Hydra heads before they split off into their own separate beings. Belly Mouth: Karen's "main" monitor is in their chest, becoming dormant when she transforms but very briefly re-emerging to order the other Karens to split off. Blue Means Smart One: Super Smart Karen has blue facial lines and is theEvil Geniusof the trio. Combining Mecha: They fuse with New Karen into an even stronger, four-headed form. Alsoinvertedin that they later each split off into separate minions along with the "main" Karen. Deadpan Snarker: Super Snarky Karen, who is snarky to both Plankton and her other heads alike.

characters.name: New Karen
characters.description: Animal Motifs: She is very much like a gorilla, walking on her knuckles,pounding her chestand making simian noises before attacking. The Baby of the Bunch: She is not only the youngest and smallest of the Karen heads, but also the most childish, topped with a high pitched voice. She also acts like anAnnoyingly Repetitive Childwho gets aBig "SHUT UP!"from the other Karens for repeating the word "Potato" nonstop. Dumb Muscle: The largest and strongest of the separate Karens seen during the movie, but also the dumbest as she runs off the most primitive technology. When she becomes part of Hydra Karen, the gestalt gains one of her huge, gorilla-like arms. From Bad to Worse: She ends up making Karen more powerful by becomingher fourth head. Fusion Dance: She and Hydra Karen's first formliterallydance with each other before combining.

characters.name: Roommate
characters.description: Devious Dolphins: Downplayed; he's not so much evil as he is aJerk Jockwho mistook Plankton for a cockroach and tried to step on him. Disposing of a Body: Played with. While it'sHarmless Freezing, Plankton and Karen hide away his frozen body in a closet with various items. Later, Plankton passes it off as a science project, whichSpongeBobbelieves. Human Popsicle: Or rather Dolphin Popsicle. He spends 25 years in a block of ice, but is sentient enough to begSpongeBoband Plankton to free him andenjoys a Krabby Pattyonce he finally thaws out. Jerk Jock: A muscular jock who doesn't even notice Plankton during most of his college life and then tried to crush him when he finallydoesnotice him. No Name Given: His name is never revealed, but Plankton nicknames him "Roomie" before putting him back in the closet.

characters.name: Barb
characters.description: Cartoony Eyes: She can extend her good eye out to use as a makeshift telescope. Deadpan Snarker: Gets a few jabs in throughout the film. The Dragon: As the Flying Dutchman's first mate, she's the secondary antagonist of the film.Until he betrays her, then she switches sides. Earn Your Happy Ending:Once the Flying Dutchman is defeated, she takes over as the Captain. Well deserved considering how she advisedSpongeBobon how to reverse the curse. Heel–Face Turn: Played with;While she certainly loses all respect for the Flying Dutchman and helps our yellow hero, she’s still a demonic ghost fish.

characters.name: Rusty Scupper
characters.description: Cash Gate:In Jellyfish Fields, he'll only giveSpongeBobhis Reef Blower if he has collected 100 jellyfish.In Goo Lagoon, he serves as an order placer for shipments and asks for 300 sand dollars to allowSpongeBobaccess to the pier. In Jellyfish Fields, he'll only giveSpongeBobhis Reef Blower if he has collected 100 jellyfish. In Goo Lagoon, he serves as an order placer for shipments and asks for 300 sand dollars to allowSpongeBobaccess to the pier. Fetch Quest: He sponsors the jellyfishing competition in Jellyfish Fields and requires 100 total jellyfish in order forSpongeBobto gain access to his Reef Blower 2500 inside his corral. Kindhearted Cat Lover: Or the setting's equivalent. He cares for a large number of retired racing snails.

characters.name: Prawn
characters.description: Amazing Technicolor Wildlife: He's a blue prawn. Justified, as prawns and other crustaceanscanbe blue when they're alive, as opposed to thered colorthey're usually depicted with. Backpack Cannon: One that has a large instrument-like horn sticking out, letting him blastSpongeBobwith damaging soundwaves. Canon Immigrant: After originating as a boss in theBattle for Bikini Bottomvideo game and a cameo in the subsequent gameTruth or Square, he was given a small cameo on the show proper in Season 13’s "Captain Pipsqueak". Cryo-Prison: Subjected to being cryogenically frozen for his crimes before accidentally being freed just like Man Ray before him in the show. Unlike Man Ray, he's frozen again after being defeated in battle. A Dog Named "Dog": A prawn named Prawn.

characters.name: Robo-Sandy
characters.description: Achilles' Heel: The robot'sloose headis her weak point which is prone to being knocked off bySpongeBoband Patrick'sGround Poundattacks and launched into loose high voltage electrical wiring. What ultimately puts her down is the giant off-switch hidden on the bottom side of her head which takes three hits fromSpongeBobin the last phase to activate. Bring It: Tauntingly does the hand motion for this is if she lands a hit onSpongeBobor Patrick. Disc-One Final Boss: She is the first major bossSpongeBobhas to defeat in order to unlock the second area of Bikini Bottom. Evil Knockoff: She is a giant robot based off Sandy Cheeks. Giant Space Flea from Nowhere: Robo-Sandy doesn't have any relevance to the plot of the game and only shows up as the first of the major three robot bosses to fight.

characters.name: Robo-Patrick
characters.description: Achilles' Heel: The "Kick me!" sign on his back, whichSpongeBobassumes is hiding some sort of self-destruct button. We never get a close enough look underneath it to tell for sure but the heroes' attacks on it prove to be effective anyway. Ax-Crazy: Robo-Patrick is the most unhinged of the three robot bosses as he wants to eat Squidward (andSpongeBob) for dessert. Boss Arena Urgency: Over the course of the second phase, each time he takes damage he pulls a chain hanging from the ceiling that releases toxic goo into the field. While Robo-Patrick himself is immune to it, Sandy has to use crates that drop when she lassos swing hooks as platforms to get to Robo-Patrick’s back with when he is dizzy. At the start of the third and final phase, Robo-Patrick breaks the chain, but by then only the highest platforms on the outside are not submerged, meaningSpongeBobhas to hit the back when Robo-Patrick is dizzy with the Bubble Bowl from a distance. Breath Weapon: He can spew an ice breath attack that's capable of freezing opponents and victims alike. He only starts using it gameplay-wise in the final phase, where it leavesSpongeBoban easy target for an ice cream shot if it hits him. Defeat Equals Explosion: AfterSpongeBoblands the final blow, he screams in pain and explodes.

characters.name: SpongeBot SteelPants
characters.description: Achilles' Heel:SpongeBothas numerous exposed lights all over his body which are prime targets forSpongeBob's Cruise Bubble. All There in the Script: The robot is not named in the original console version; it receives its name in the Game Boy Advance port, and was finally named in the awards ofRehydrated. The Dragon: Serves as one for Robo-Plankton. Dual Boss: In the first phase, he is fought alongside Robo-Plankton. Evil Knockoff: He is a giant robot based offSpongeBob SquarePants.

characters.name: Robo-Plankton
characters.description: Battle Couple: AssistsSpongeBotin his first boss fight and they are apprently engaged. Big Bad: He usurps this role from Plankton himself and becomes the main villain at the end of the game. Camp Gay:Played for Laughs. Robo-Plankton talks about marryingSpongeBot SteelPantsand retains all of regular Plankton's campiness and theatricality. Dual Boss: In the first phase, he is fought alongsideSpongeBot SteelPants. Energy Weapon: His hovercraft is equipped with a rapid-firing laser weapon.

characters.name: Gill Hammerstein
characters.description: His involvement with the story differs from the different ports with the game. In the consoles, he placesSpongeBoband his crew against each other to see who can get which role in the episode. In the PC port, he needsSpongeBob's help to get a crew for the new episode. In the Game Boy Advance port, he needsSpongeBob's help to find Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy as he can get filming of the new episode done with. Game-Over Man: If none of the players manage to reach the required popularity points in a location by the final minigame, Gill will get angry and force them to redo the auditions until one of them succeeds. Prima Donna Director: While he may seem affable on the surface, Gill is a perfectionist and will get temperamental if his quota isn't met. He'll even outright demand the participants to redo the audition minigames from scratch if they fail to reach the point threshold needed for the role. Same Character, But Different: Gill's role in both console and PC ports are the same as well as his voice actor, but his personality and voice are different from each other. In the console, Gill is calm, sarcastic and a bit nerdy due to his lisp. His PC counterpart is much more louder and mean. Threatening Shark:Gill is rather calm in the console ports, though if the player doesn't get enough points, that's when he gets a bit upset and demands them to try again.His PC counterpart comes across as this due to his loud voice and nasty attitude.

characters.name: The Sneaky Hermit
characters.description: Big Bad: He's the main villain of the game'sShow Within a Showwho wants to steal every home in Bikini Bottom. Freudian Excuse: The reason he wants to steal every building is because his ex-wife took the house in their divorce, leaving him without a home and turning him to villainy as a result. Static Role, Exchangeable Character: The Sneaky Hermit can be played by any of the six main characters if they accumulate enough total audition points and beat the rest of the competition by the end of the story campaign. As a result, the Sneaky Hermit's personality can vary drastically, ranging fromSpongeBob's goofiness to Plankton's melodrama. Weaksauce Weakness:His nose is very sensitive to peppers. Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy defeat the Sneaky Hermit this way by spraying pepper on him andmaking him sneeze, causing him to drop all of his stolen buildings back into their original spots.

characters.name: Dreaded Patrick
characters.description: Arc Villain: He serves as the main villain in "Starfishman to the Rescue". The Bad Guy Wins: While morePlayed for Laughs, at the end of the level, Dreaded Patrick successfully baits Starfishman to the rocket, have his minions knock him out, performs the old switcheroo with the hostage and launches Starfishman into space. This is evenlampshadedby both Starfishman (who notes thatThe Good Guys Always Win), and Dreaded Patrick himself (who is forced into aAnd Then What?situation about what to do next). As aDouble Subversion, Dreaded Patrick still gets some karmic retribution in the end as a doughnut-shaped meteor the rocket hits on its way out falls to Earth and traps him in it. Even Evil Has Standards: In Nighty Nightmare, he refuses to set up traps in an evil lair in favor of simply putting Starfishman in his own dirty house, out of sheer disgust at how unkempt the place is. Evil Counterpart: He's essentially just an evil version of Patrick in a world full of starfish citizens who look and sound like him. Large Ham: Even by Bill Fagerbakke's standards, Dreaded Patrick speaks entirely in a deep, overly-hammy voice to emphasize his role as a supervillain.

characters.name: The Village Chief
characters.description: Companion Cube: The Chief has an ironing board for a wife, of whom he sees as "pretty pretty". It later gets subverted whenSpongeBobrescues "her" and the Chief realizes that he doesn't find her pretty pretty anymore, and so he insistsSpongeBobto take the ironing board with him as a useful plane part. Large and in Charge: He's the biggest and most top-heavy member of the castaways, which signifies his position as the village chief.

characters.name: The Inventor
characters.description: Creepy Good: Despite the Inventor's awkward mannerisms and implications that he desperately wantsSpongeBobas his lab assistant/test subject, he's an otherwise nice guy who will giveSpongeBobhelpful hints on his journey and provides him with another plane part in return. Fetch Quest: His primary task forSpongeBobis for him to take back the three jellyfish power cells, which were stolen by the worm crustaceans and locked deep inside his three workshops. Gadgeteer Genius: He's the inventor of the jellyfish-powered device that makes him the perfect cup of tea. Some of his other inventions mentioned in his dialogue also include "a telephone", a seismic back scrubber and a pair of untested rocket pants. Mission Control: He providesSpongeBobwith hints from his lab as he searches through the Inventor's workshops for his jellyfish power cells.

characters.name: Doodle Patrick
characters.description: Bullfight Boss: His simplest attack is to charge atDoodlepantsuntil he hits a wall. He's actually entirely vulnerable during this attack. Charged Attack: One of his attacks is to pause and lean back with a menacing glare before chucking Doodle Goo at Doodlepants. He's vulnerable during the charge which interrupts the attack completely. Combat Breakdown: Despite his intelligence, as aBoss Fighthe's reduced to brute force tactics none too different from the real Patrick Star. Heeven pounds his chest like a gorillathroughout the fight and is shown tostill suck his thumb whenever he's stunned. Seems he'sNot So Above It Allafter all. The Dragon:Maybe.He states that he's following some sort of mission, presumably given to him byDoodleBobthough he doesn't really say enough to confirm what his exact relationship toDoodleBobis or what he's even trying to accomplish. All we know is that hedistracts the heroesandantagonizes thembefore beingerased entirely. Evil Genius: Much more of a schemer compared toDoodleBob, manipulating the Flying Dutchman into antagonizing the heroes and then later commandeering his Ghost Ship while he's distracted.

characters.name: Seymour Scales
characters.description: Alliterative Name:SeymourScales. Big Bad: OfBoating Bash, as it is revealed that he has been manipulatingSpongeBobfor the whole game all for the sake of money. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Initially appears to be a kindly old boating instructor, but only cares about takingSpongeBob's money by tricking him into joining his sham classes. Broken Pedestal:SpongeBobis utterlybrokenupon learning Seymour's true intentions. Con Man: His entire class is nothing but a grand scam to get a rather gullibleSpongeBobto pay more money. Some of the other characters like Mr. Krabs and Mrs. Puff were quick to figure this out, but the reason they fail to tellSpongeBobearly is because the former is swayed by money talk, while the latter goes incognito to investigate the whole thing.
